sentences.zh: 【齊紀五】 閼逢閹茂，一年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 5] Eyan cycle, Emao year, one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 5] The Emao year of the Eyan cycle, year one.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝上建武元年（

translations.literal: First year of Jianwu of Emperor Ming the High Ancestor, upper fascicle (
translations.idiomatic: The first year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming the High Ancestor (upper fascicle) (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元四九四年）

translations.literal: jiaxu, AD 494)
translations.idiomatic: jiaxu, AD 494)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未，改元隆昌；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day dingwei, the era name was changed to Longchang;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the dingwei day of the first month, the era name was changed to Longchang;

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史晉安王子懋，以主幼時艱，密為自全之計，令作部造仗；

translations.literal: Xiao Mao, Prince of Jin'an and governor of Yong Province, because the ruler was young and times were perilous, secretly made plans to secure himself, ordering his headquarters to manufacture weapons;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mao, Prince of Jin'an and governor of Yong Province, seeing that the sovereign was young and the times precarious, secretly laid plans for his own safety and ordered his headquarters to forge arms;

sentences.zh: 征南大將軍陳顯達屯襄陽，子懋欲脅取以為將。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda, Grand General Who Conquers the South, was stationed at Xiangyang; Zimao wished to coerce him into serving as his commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda, Grand General Who Conquers the South, was encamped at Xiangyang, and the prince hoped to coerce him into taking command on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 顯達密啟西昌侯鸞，鸞征顯達為車騎大將軍；

translations.literal: Xianda secretly reported to Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang; Luan summoned Xianda to be Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Xianda secretly informed Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang, whereupon Luan recalled him to court as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 徙子懋為江州刺史，仍令留部曲助鎮襄陽，單將白直、俠轂自隨。

translations.literal: He transferred Zimao to be governor of Jiang Province, yet still ordered him to leave his troops to help garrison Xiangyang, going alone with only his personal guards and armed retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned the prince to governor of Jiang Province but still required him to leave his troops to help hold Xiangyang, allowing him to depart with only his household guards and armed followers.

sentences.zh: 顯達過襄陽，子懋謂曰：「朝廷令身單身而返，身是天王，豈可過爾輕率！

translations.literal: When Xianda passed through Xiangyang, Zimao said to him: "The court orders me to return alone in person—I am a Son of Heaven; how can I be so lightly treated!
translations.idiomatic: As Xianda passed through Xiangyang, the prince said to him, "The court orders me to return unaccompanied. I am a Son of Heaven—how can they treat me so lightly!

sentences.zh: 今猶欲將二三千人自隨，公意何如？」

translations.literal: I still wish to take two or three thousand men with me—what is your opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: I still mean to take two or three thousand men with me. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 顯達曰：「殿下若不留部曲，乃是大違敕旨，其事不輕；

translations.literal: Xianda said: "If Your Highness does not leave your troops behind, that is a grave violation of the imperial order, and the matter is no light one;
translations.idiomatic: Xianda replied, "If Your Highness does not leave your troops behind, you will be in grave breach of the imperial command;

sentences.zh: 且此間人亦難可收用。」

translations.literal: moreover, the men here would also be hard to employ."
translations.idiomatic: and besides, the men here would be difficult to rely on."

sentences.zh: 子懋默然。

translations.literal: Zimao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said nothing.

sentences.zh: 顯達因辭出，即發去。

translations.literal: Xianda took his leave and departed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda took his leave and set out immediately.

sentences.zh: 子懋計未立，乃之尋陽。

translations.literal: Zimao's plans were not yet settled, so he went on to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His plans still unsettled, the prince proceeded to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞將謀廢立，引前鎮西咨議參軍蕭衍與同謀。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was about to plot deposition and enthronement; he drew in Xiao Yan, former staff adviser of the Army That Guards the West, to conspire with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was preparing to depose the emperor and enthrone another, and enlisted Xiao Yan, formerly a staff adviser on the western command, as his co-conspirator.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史隨王子隆，性溫和，有文才；

translations.literal: Xiao Zilong, Prince of Sui and governor of Jing Province, was mild in nature and gifted in letters;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zilong, Prince of Sui and governor of Jing Province, was gentle by nature and accomplished in letters;

sentences.zh: 鸞欲征之，恐其不從。

translations.literal: Luan wished to summon him but feared he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Luan wished to recall him to court but feared he would refuse.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「隨王雖有美名，其實庸劣。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Although the Prince of Sui has a fine reputation, in truth he is mediocre and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "The Prince of Sui may enjoy a fine reputation, but in truth he is mediocre.

sentences.zh: 既無智謀之士，爪牙唯仗司馬垣歷生、武陵太守卞白龍耳。

translations.literal: He has no men of wisdom and stratagem; his claws and teeth rely solely on Chief Administrator Yuan Lisheng and Bian Bailong, governor of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He has no counselors of real ability; he depends entirely on his chief administrator Yuan Lisheng and Bian Bailong, governor of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 二人唯利是從，若啖以顯職，無有不來；

translations.literal: The two follow only profit; if tempted with prominent office, there is none who would not come;
translations.idiomatic: Both men follow profit alone—offer them high office and they will surely come;

sentences.zh: 隨王止須折簡耳。」

translations.literal: the Prince of Sui need only receive a brief letter."
translations.idiomatic: as for the prince himself, a single summons will suffice."

sentences.zh: 鸞從之。

translations.literal: Luan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Luan followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 征歷生為太子左衛率，白龍為游擊將軍；

translations.literal: He summoned Lisheng to be Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and Bailong to be General Who Attacks in All Directions;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yuan to be Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and Bian to be General Who Attacks in All Directions;

sentences.zh: 二人並至。

translations.literal: both men arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Both men came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 續召子隆為侍中、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He then summoned Zilong to be Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled the prince to serve as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史崔慧景，高、武舊將，鸞疑之，以蕭衍為寧朔將軍，戍壽陽。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, governor of Yu Province, was an old general of Emperors Gao and Wu; Luan was suspicious of him and appointed Xiao Yan General Who Pacifies the North and stationed him at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing, governor of Yu Province, was a veteran of the Gao and Wu reigns; Luan distrusted him and posted Xiao Yan as General Who Pacifies the North at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 慧景懼，白服出迎；

translations.literal: Huijing was afraid and came out to meet him in white dress;
translations.idiomatic: Cui, alarmed, came out to meet him dressed in white;

sentences.zh: 衍撫安之。

translations.literal: Yan comforted and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan reassured and calmed him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，鬱林王祀南郊；

translations.literal: On day xinhai, Emperor Yulin sacrificed at the Southern Suburb;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, Emperor Yulin performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 戊午，拜崇安陵。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, he paid homage at Chong'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day, he paid his respects at Chong'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏主南巡；

translations.literal: On day guihai, the Wei sovereign made a southern tour;
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, the Wei emperor toured south;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，過比干墓，祭以太牢，魏主自為祝文曰：「烏呼介士，胡不我臣！」

translations.literal: On day wuchen, passing the tomb of Bi Gan, he sacrificed with the great offering; the Wei sovereign himself composed the prayer text, saying: "Alas, steadfast knight—why did you not serve me as subject!"
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, passing the tomb of Bi Gan, he offered the great sacrifice; the emperor himself composed the prayer, saying, "Alas, steadfast knight—why would you not serve me as your lord!"

sentences.zh: 帝寵幸中書舍人綦毌珍之、朱隆之、直閣將軍曹道剛、周奉叔、宦者徐龍駒等。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Palace Secretariat Attendants Qi Wuzhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, Direct Gate Generals Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu, and the eunuch Xu Longju, among others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lavished favor on Palace Secretariat Attendants Qi Wuzhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, Direct Gate Generals Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu, and the eunuch Xu Longju, among others.

sentences.zh: 珍之所論薦，事無不允；

translations.literal: Whatever Zhenzhi recommended was never denied;
translations.idiomatic: Nothing Zhenzhi recommended was ever refused;

sentences.zh: 內外要職，皆先論價，旬月之間，家累千金；

translations.literal: for important posts inside and outside the court, prices were first negotiated; within ten days or a month his household amassed thousands in gold;
translations.idiomatic: for every important post inside and outside the court he fixed a price first; within weeks his household had amassed thousands in gold;

sentences.zh: 擅取官物及役作，不俟詔旨。

translations.literal: he seized government goods and labor on his own authority, without awaiting imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: he seized government property and corvée labor at will, without awaiting imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 有司至相語云：「寧拒至尊敕，不可違舍人命。」

translations.literal: Officials even said to one another: "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's command than to disobey the Secretariat Attendant's word."
translations.idiomatic: Officials even said to one another, "Better to defy the emperor's command than to disobey the Secretariat Attendant."

sentences.zh: 帝以龍駒為後閣舍人，常居含章蓼，著黃綸帽，被貂裘，南面向案，代帝畫敕；

translations.literal: The emperor made Longju a Rear Pavilion Attendant; he constantly dwelt in the Hanzhang quarter, wore a yellow silk cap and a sable fur coat, faced south toward the desk, and drafted edicts in the emperor's place;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Longju a Rear Pavilion Attendant; he lived permanently in the Hanzhang quarter, wore a yellow silk cap and sable fur, faced south at the desk, and drafted edicts in the emperor's stead;

sentences.zh: 左右侍直，與帝不異。

translations.literal: attendants stood at his side no differently than for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: with attendants standing by his side no differently than for the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 帝自山陵之後，即與左右微服遊走市裡，好於世宗崇安陵隧中擲塗、賭跳，作諸鄙戲，極意賞賜左右，動至百數十萬。

translations.literal: After the imperial tombs, the emperor at once went with his attendants in disguise to roam the markets; he delighted in throwing mud, gambling at jumping, and other vulgar games in the tunnel of Emperor Shizong's Chong'an Mausoleum, lavishing rewards on his attendants to the extent of hundreds of thousands or millions.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral rites, the emperor went about the markets in disguise with his attendants; he delighted in flinging mud, gambling at hopscotch, and other coarse games in the tunnel of Emperor Shizong's Chong'an Mausoleum, rewarding his companions extravagantly—often in sums of hundreds of thousands or millions.

sentences.zh: 每見錢，曰：「我昔思汝一枚不得，今日得用汝未？」

translations.literal: Whenever he saw money he would say: "I once longed for you by the piece and could not have you—today, may I use you at last?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw money he would say, "I once longed for you coin by coin and could not have you—today, may I use you at last?"

sentences.zh: 世祖聚錢上庫五億萬，齋庫亦出三億萬，金銀布帛不可勝計；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had amassed five hundred million in the upper treasury and three hundred million in the palace treasury as well, with gold, silver, silk, and cloth beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu had amassed five hundred million coins in the upper treasury and three hundred million more in the palace treasury, with gold, silver, silk, and cloth beyond reckoning;

sentences.zh: 鬱林王即位未期歲，所用垂盡。

translations.literal: before a full year of Emperor Yulin's reign, nearly all was spent.
translations.idiomatic: yet before a full year of Yulin's reign, nearly all of it was gone.

sentences.zh: 入主衣庫，令何後及寵姬以諸寶器相投擊破碎之，用為笑樂。

translations.literal: He entered the imperial wardrobe treasury and ordered Empress He and his favorite concubines to hurl precious vessels at one another until they shattered, taking this as sport and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the imperial wardrobe treasury and had Empress He and his favorite concubines smash precious vessels against one another for amusement.

sentences.zh: 蒸於世祖幸姬霍氏，更其姓曰徐。

translations.literal: He took as consort Huo, a favored concubine of Emperor Shizu, and changed her surname to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Huo, a favored concubine of Emperor Shizu, as his own and changed her surname to Xu.

sentences.zh: 朝事大小，皆決於西昌侯鸞。

translations.literal: Matters great and small at court were all decided by Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small affairs of state were all decided by Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang.

sentences.zh: 鸞數諫爭，帝多不從；

translations.literal: Luan remonstrated repeatedly, but the emperor mostly would not heed him;
translations.idiomatic: Luan remonstrated again and again, but the emperor mostly refused to listen;

sentences.zh: 心忌鸞，欲除之。

translations.literal: in his heart he resented Luan and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: he came to resent Luan and wished to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射鄱陽王鏘為世祖所厚，私謂鏘曰：「公聞鸞於法身如何？」

translations.literal: Because Xiao Zheng, Prince of Poyang and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, had been favored by Emperor Shizu, the emperor said privately to Zheng: "Have you heard what Luan is like toward Fashen?"
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiao Zheng, Prince of Poyang and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, had been favored by Emperor Shizu, the emperor said privately to him, "What have you heard of Luan's attitude toward Fashen?"

sentences.zh: 鏘素和謹，對曰：「臣鸞於宗戚最長，且受寄先帝；

translations.literal: Zheng was by nature mild and cautious and replied: "Your servant—Luan is the eldest among the imperial clansmen and moreover received the late emperor's trust;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, mild and cautious by nature, replied, "Luan is the senior among our kinsmen and was entrusted by the late emperor;

sentences.zh: 臣等皆年少，朝廷所損，唯鸞一人，願陛下無以為慮。」

translations.literal: we are all young; of those the court can afford to lose, Luan alone would suffice—may Your Majesty have no concern on this account."
translations.idiomatic: we are all young; of those the court can afford to lose, only Luan would matter—Your Majesty need not worry on that account."

sentences.zh: 帝退，謂徐龍駒曰：「我欲與公共計取鸞，公既不同，我不能獨辦，且復小聽。」

translations.literal: The emperor withdrew and said to Xu Longju: "I wished to join with you in plotting to take Luan; since you do not agree, I cannot act alone—let us wait a little longer yet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew and said to Xu Longju, "I wanted to plot with you to take Luan down; since you will not agree, I cannot act alone—for now we must wait a little longer."

sentences.zh: 衛尉蕭諶，世祖之族子也，自世祖在郢州，諶已為腹心。

translations.literal: Xiao Chen, Commandant of the Guards, was a clansman of Emperor Shizu; from the time Shizu was at Ying Province, Chen had been his trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen, Commandant of the Guards, was a kinsman of Emperor Shizu; from the time Shizu held Ying Province, Chen had been his intimate confidant.

sentences.zh: 及即位，常典宿衛，機密之事，無不預聞。

translations.literal: When Yulin ascended the throne, Chen constantly managed the night guard; in confidential matters there was none in which he did not share.
translations.idiomatic: After Yulin's accession, Chen constantly commanded the night guard and was privy to every confidential matter.

sentences.zh: 征南咨議蕭坦之，諶之族人也，嘗為東宮直閣，為世宗所知。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi, staff adviser of the Army That Conquers the South, was also Chen's kinsman; he had once been a Direct Gate officer in the Eastern Palace and was known to Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi, staff adviser on the southern command, was Chen's kinsman as well; he had once served as a Direct Gate officer in the Eastern Palace and was known to Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 帝以二人祖父舊人，甚親信之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the two were old associates of his grandfather, trusted them deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, regarding them as old associates of his grandfather's circle, trusted them deeply.

sentences.zh: 諶每請急出宿，帝通夕不寐，諶還乃安。

translations.literal: Whenever Chen asked to leave on urgent business to lodge outside, the emperor could not sleep all night; only when Chen returned would he be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chen asked leave to lodge outside, the emperor lay awake all night and slept only after Chen returned.

sentences.zh: 坦之得出入後宮。

translations.literal: Tanzhi was permitted to enter and leave the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was permitted free access to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝褻狎宴游，坦之皆在側。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor indulged in familiar revelry and sport, Tanzhi was always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor indulged in intimate revelry, Tanzhi was always present.

sentences.zh: 帝醉後，常裸袒，坦之輒扶持諫諭。

translations.literal: When the emperor was drunk he often stripped bare; Tanzhi would always support him and admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: When drunk the emperor often stripped to the waist; Tanzhi would steady him and remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞欲有所諫，帝在後宮不出，唯遣諶、坦之徑進，乃得聞達。

translations.literal: When Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang, wished to remonstrate, the emperor would not come out of the rear palace; only by sending Chen and Tanzhi straight in could his words reach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan wished to remonstrate, the emperor would not leave the inner palace; only by sending Chen and Tanzhi directly in could his words reach him.

sentences.zh: 何後亦淫泆，私於帝左右楊鈱，與同寢處如伉儷；

translations.literal: Empress He was also dissolute; she had a private affair with Yang Qian, an attendant at the emperor's side, and slept with him as man and wife;
translations.idiomatic: Empress He was dissolute as well; she took Yang Qian, an attendant at the emperor's side, as her lover and slept with him as man and wife;

sentences.zh: 又與帝相愛狎，故帝恣之。

translations.literal: she was also intimate with the emperor, so he indulged her freely.
translations.idiomatic: she was also intimate with the emperor himself, who therefore indulged her without restraint.

sentences.zh: 迎後親戚入宮，以耀靈殿處之。

translations.literal: She brought her kinsmen into the palace and lodged them in the Yaoling Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She brought her relatives into the palace and housed them in the Yaoling Hall.

sentences.zh: 齋閣通夜洞開，外內淆雜，無復分別。

translations.literal: The fasting chambers stood open all night; inside and outside were confused together with no distinction left.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting chambers stood open all night; inner and outer quarters were mingled without distinction.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞遣坦之入奏誅鈱，何後流涕覆面曰：「楊郎好年少，無罪，何可枉殺！」

translations.literal: Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang, sent Tanzhi in to report and have Qian executed; Empress He wept, covering her face, and said: "Young Master Yang is so fine and young—he is innocent; how can he be killed unjustly!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan sent Tanzhi in to petition for Qian's execution; the empress wept, covering her face, and said, "Young Master Yang is so fine and young—he is innocent; how can you kill him unjustly!"

sentences.zh: 坦之附耳語帝曰：「外間並雲楊鈱與皇后有情，事彰遐邇，不可不誅。」

translations.literal: Tanzhi whispered in the emperor's ear: "Outside, all say Yang Qian has relations with the empress; the matter is known far and near—it cannot go unpunished."
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi whispered in the emperor's ear, "Outside, everyone says Yang Qian and the empress are lovers; the affair is known far and wide—he cannot go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已許之；

translations.literal: The emperor, having no choice, consented;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no choice, consented;

sentences.zh: 俄敕原之，已行刑矣。

translations.literal: soon an edict pardoned him—but the execution had already been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: but scarcely had an edict of pardon been issued when the execution was already done.

sentences.zh: 鸞又啟誅徐龍駒，帝亦不能違，而心忌鸞益甚。

translations.literal: Luan again memorialized to have Xu Longju executed; the emperor likewise could not refuse, yet resented Luan all the more in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Luan again petitioned for Xu Longju's execution; the emperor could not refuse, yet resented Luan all the more.

sentences.zh: 蕭諶、蕭坦之見帝狂縱日甚，無復悛改，恐禍及己，乃更回意附鸞，勸其廢立，陰為鸞耳目，帝不之覺也。

translations.literal: Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi, seeing the emperor's wild excess grow daily with no sign of reform, feared disaster would reach them; they therefore turned again to attach themselves to Luan, urging him to depose and enthrone, and secretly served as Luan's eyes and ears—the emperor did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi, seeing the emperor's excess grow worse daily with no sign of reform, feared they would be swept up in the ruin; they therefore shifted their loyalty to Luan, urged him to depose and enthrone another, and secretly served as his informants—without the emperor's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 周奉叔恃勇挾勢，陵轢公卿。

translations.literal: Zhou Fengshu relied on his courage and leveraged his power, trampling over dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fengshu, relying on his courage and the power he wielded, rode roughshod over dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 常翼單刀二十口自隨，出入禁闥，門衛不敢訶。

translations.literal: He constantly carried twenty single-edged blades at his side, entering and leaving the forbidden gates; the gate guards dared not reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly carried twenty blades at his side, passing in and out of the forbidden gates while the guards dared not challenge him.

sentences.zh: 每語人曰：「周郎刀不識君！」

translations.literal: He often said to people: "Young Master Zhou's blades do not know you!"
translations.idiomatic: He would say to people, "Young Master Zhou's blades know no master but me!"

sentences.zh: 鸞忌之，使蕭諶、蕭坦之說帝出奉叔為外援。

translations.literal: Luan resented him and had Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi persuade the emperor to send Fengshu out as external support.
translations.idiomatic: Luan feared him and had Chen and Tanzhi persuade the emperor to post Fengshu outside the capital as a military ally.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以奉叔為青州刺史，曹道剛為中軍司馬。

translations.literal: On day jisi, Fengshu was made governor of Qing Province and Cao Daogang was made Army Supervisor of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Fengshu was appointed governor of Qing Province and Cao Daogang Army Supervisor of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 奉叔就帝求千戶侯；

translations.literal: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of a thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of a thousand households;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: which the emperor granted.

sentences.zh: 鸞以為不可，封曲江縣男，食三百戶。

translations.literal: Luan held this impossible and enfeoffed him as Baron of Qujiang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Luan would not allow it and enfeoffed him instead as Baron of Qujiang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 奉叔大怒，於眾中攘刀厲色；

translations.literal: Fengshu was furious and brandished his blade with a fierce countenance before the assembly;
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu flew into a rage and brandished his blade with a fierce look before the whole court;

sentences.zh: 鸞說諭之，乃受。

translations.literal: Luan persuaded and instructed him, and he then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Luan talked him round, and he accepted.

sentences.zh: 奉叔辭畢，將之鎮，部伍已出。

translations.literal: When Fengshu had taken his leave and was about to depart for his post, his troops had already gone out.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his leave, Fengshu was about to depart for his post; his troops had already marched out.

sentences.zh: 鸞與蕭諶稱敕，召奉叔於省中，毆殺之，啟云：「奉叔慢朝廷。」

translations.literal: Luan and Xiao Chen, in the emperor's name, summoned Fengshu to the Secretariat and beat him to death, reporting: "Fengshu showed contempt for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Luan and Xiao Chen, invoking an imperial order, summoned Fengshu to the Secretariat and beat him to death, reporting that "Fengshu showed contempt for the court."

sentences.zh: 帝不獲已，可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no choice, approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, powerless to refuse, approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 溧陽令錢唐杜文謙，嘗為南郡王侍讀，前此說綦毋珍之曰：「天下事可知，灰燼粉滅，匪朝伊夕；

translations.literal: Du Wenqian of Qiantang, magistrate of Liyang, had once been tutor to the Prince of Nan commandery; earlier he had said to Qi Wuzhenzhi: "The affairs of the realm can be foreseen—reduced to ashes and dust, not a morning or evening away;
translations.idiomatic: Du Wenqian of Qiantang, magistrate of Liyang, had once served as tutor to the Prince of Nan commandery; he had earlier said to Qi Wuzhenzhi, "The realm's fate is plain—all will be ashes before long;

sentences.zh: 不早為計，吾徒無類矣。」

translations.literal: if we do not plan early, our sort will leave no survivors."
translations.idiomatic: if we do not act soon, men like us will not survive."

sentences.zh: 珍之曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: Zhenzhi said: "What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi asked, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 文謙曰：「先帝舊人，多見擯斥，今召而使之，誰不慷慨！

translations.literal: Wenqian said: "The late emperor's old men have mostly been cast aside; summon them now and employ them—who would not burn with zeal!
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian said, "The late emperor's old followers have mostly been cast aside—recall them now and who would not rise eagerly!

sentences.zh: 近聞王洪範與宿衛將萬靈會等共語，皆攘袂捶床；

translations.literal: I have lately heard Wang Hongfan speaking together with the palace guard general Wan Linghui and others—all rolled up their sleeves and beat the bed;
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that Wang Hongfan and the palace guard general Wan Linghui and others, talking together, rolled up their sleeves and pounded the bed;

sentences.zh: 君其密報周奉叔，使萬靈會等殺蕭諶，則宮內之兵皆我用也。

translations.literal: you should secretly inform Zhou Fengshu and have Wan Linghui and the rest kill Xiao Chen—then all the troops within the palace will be ours to use.
translations.idiomatic: secretly inform Zhou Fengshu and have Wan Linghui and the rest kill Xiao Chen—then every soldier in the palace will be ours.

sentences.zh: 即勒兵入尚書，斬蕭令，兩都伯力耳。

translations.literal: Then lead the troops into the Imperial Secretariat and behead Minister Xiao—it is only the strength of two commandery chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Then march on the Imperial Secretariat and behead Minister Xiao—it is only the work of two commandery chiefs.

sentences.zh: 今舉大事亦死，不舉事亦死；

translations.literal: Now to undertake the great affair is also death, and not to undertake it is also death;
translations.idiomatic: Act now and you die; fail to act and you die likewise;

sentences.zh: 二死等耳，死社稷可乎！

translations.literal: the two deaths are equal—may we not die for the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: the two deaths are equal—why not die for the altars of state!

sentences.zh: 若遲疑不斷，復少日，錄君稱敕賜死，父母為殉，在眼中矣。」

translations.literal: If you hesitate and cannot decide, in a few more days the Secretariat Attendant will issue an edict in the emperor's name granting you death, with your parents as companions in death—it is before your eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate a few days more and the Secretariat Attendant will issue an edict in the emperor's name ordering your death, your parents dying with you—it is already in sight."

sentences.zh: 珍之不能用。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi could not adopt this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi would not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 及鸞殺奉叔，並收珍之、文謙，殺之。

translations.literal: When Luan killed Fengshu, he also seized Zhenzhi and Wenqian and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan killed Fengshu, he also arrested Zhenzhi and Wenqian and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏主如洛陽西宮。

translations.literal: On day yihai, the Wei sovereign went to the Western Palace at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, the Wei emperor went to the Western Palace at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎韓顯宗上書陳四事：其一以為：「竊聞輿駕今夏不巡三齊，當幸中山。

translations.literal: Han Xianzong, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, submitted a memorial setting forth four matters: the first held that: "I have heard privately that this summer the imperial carriage will not tour the Three Qi but will visit Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xianzong, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, submitted a memorial on four matters. The first stated, "I have heard that this summer Your Majesty will not tour the Three Qi but will visit Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 往冬輿駕停鄴，當農隙之時，猶比屋供奉，不勝勞費。

translations.literal: Last winter the imperial carriage halted at Ye, at a time of agricultural slack, yet every household still had to supply provisions, unable to bear the labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter the imperial progress halted at Ye, during the agricultural slack season, yet every household was still pressed to supply provisions beyond what they could bear.

sentences.zh: 況今蠶麥方急，將何以堪命！

translations.literal: How much more now, when silkworms and wheat are urgently at hand—how can the people bear the burden!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can they bear it now, when silkworms and wheat demand their utmost attention!

sentences.zh: 且六軍涉暑，恐生癘疫。

translations.literal: Moreover, the six armies passing through summer heat may breed pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the six armies marching in summer heat may breed pestilence.

sentences.zh: 臣願早還北京，以省諸州供張之苦，成洛都營繕之役。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes an early return to the Northern Capital, to spare the provinces the hardship of provisioning, and to complete the construction work at the Luo capital."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to return early to the Northern Capital, to spare the provinces the burden of provisioning and to complete the construction at Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 其二以為：「洛陽宮殿故基，皆魏明帝所造，前世已譏其奢。

translations.literal: The second held that: "The old foundations of the Luoyang palaces were all built by Emperor Ming of Wei; former ages already mocked their extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The second held that "the old foundations of the Luoyang palaces were all built by Emperor Ming of Wei, and former ages already mocked their extravagance.

sentences.zh: 今茲營繕，宜加裁損。

translations.literal: The present construction should be further curtailed.
translations.idiomatic: The present construction ought to be further reduced.

sentences.zh: 又，頃來北都富室，競以第捨相尚；

translations.literal: Moreover, of late the wealthy houses of the Northern Capital have vied in the grandeur of their mansions;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, of late the wealthy families of the Northern Capital have vied in the grandeur of their mansions;

sentences.zh: 宜因遷徙，為之制度。

translations.literal: the move should be used to impose regulations on them.
translations.idiomatic: the move should be used to impose regulations on them.

sentences.zh: 及端廣衢路，通利溝渠。」

translations.literal: Roads should be made straight and broad, and ditches and canals cleared for flow."
translations.idiomatic: Roads should be made straight and broad, and ditches and canals cleared for drainage."

sentences.zh: 其三以為：「陛下之還洛陽，輕將從騎。

translations.literal: The third held that: "When Your Majesty returns to Luoyang, you travel lightly with only a few mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: The third held that "when Your Majesty returns to Luoyang, you travel with only a light escort.

sentences.zh: 王者於闈闥之內施警蹕，況涉履山河而不加三思乎！」

translations.literal: A king within his inner gates applies the royal guard and prohibition—how much more when traversing mountains and rivers without triple reflection!"
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign applies the royal guard even within his inner gates—how much more when crossing mountains and rivers without careful thought!"

sentences.zh: 其四以為：「陛下耳聽法音，目玩墳典，口對百辟，心虞萬機，景昃而食，夜分而寢；

translations.literal: The fourth held that: "Your Majesty's ears hear the dharma's sound, your eyes peruse the classics of the ancients, your mouth addresses the hundred ministers, your mind attends to the myriad affairs of state—you eat at sundown and sleep after midnight;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth held that "Your Majesty's ears hear the dharma's sound, your eyes peruse the classics, your mouth addresses the hundred ministers, and your mind attends to the myriad affairs of state—you eat at sundown and sleep after midnight;

sentences.zh: 加以孝思之至，隨進而深；

translations.literal: added to this, filial remembrance deepens with every advance;
translations.idiomatic: to this is added filial remembrance, which deepens with every advance;

sentences.zh: 文章之業，日成篇卷；

translations.literal: literary work daily completes scrolls and fascicles;
translations.idiomatic: and literary work daily completes scroll upon scroll;

sentences.zh: 雖睿時所用，未足為煩，然非所以嗇神養性，保無疆之祚也。

translations.literal: though what a sage uses in his time is not enough to be called a burden, yet this is not the way to husband the spirit and nourish one's nature, or to preserve an unending reign.
translations.idiomatic: though a sage's labors are not in themselves excessive, this is not the way to husband the spirit and preserve an enduring reign.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下垂拱司契而天下治矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty might fold your hands and hold the tally, and all under Heaven would be well governed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to fold your hands in rule and let all under Heaven govern itself."

sentences.zh: 帝頗納之。

translations.literal: The emperor largely accepted these views.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 顯宗，麒麟之子也。

translations.literal: Xianzong was the son of Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was the son of Han Lin.

sentences.zh: 顯宗又上言，以為：「州郡貢察，徒有秀、孝之名，而無秀、孝之實；

translations.literal: Xianzong again submitted a memorial, holding that: "In the provincial and commandery recommendations and inspections, there are only the names of the Cultivated and Filial, without the reality of the Cultivated and Filial;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong submitted another memorial, arguing that "provincial recommendations bore only the names of the Cultivated and Filial, without the reality;

sentences.zh: 朝廷但檢其門望，不復彈坐。

translations.literal: the court only examines their family standing and no longer investigates and punishes.
translations.idiomatic: the court examined only family standing and no longer investigated misconduct.

sentences.zh: 如此，則可令別貢門望以敘士人，何假冒秀、孝之名也！

translations.literal: If so, one might as well have a separate recommendation of family standing to rank the scholar-officials—why falsely borrow the names of the Cultivated and Filial!
translations.idiomatic: In that case, one might as well recommend men by family standing alone—why falsely borrow the names of the Cultivated and Filial!

sentences.zh: 夫門望者，乃其父祖之遺烈，亦何益於皇家！

translations.literal: Family standing is but the legacy of one's father and grandfather—what benefit is it to the imperial house!
translations.idiomatic: Family standing is merely the legacy of one's forebears—what benefit is it to the throne!

sentences.zh: 益於時者，賢才而已。

translations.literal: What benefits the age is talent alone.
translations.idiomatic: What benefits the age is talent alone.

sentences.zh: 苟有其才，雖屠、釣、奴、虜，聖王不恥以為臣；

translations.literal: If one has talent, though butcher, fisherman, slave, or captive, a sage king does not disdain to make him a minister;
translations.idiomatic: If a man has talent, though he be butcher, fisherman, slave, or captive, a sage king does not disdain to make him a minister;

sentences.zh: 苟非其才，雖三後之胤，墜於皁隸矣。

translations.literal: if one lacks talent, though descendant of the three queens, he falls among the black-clad servants.
translations.idiomatic: if he lacks talent, though he be descendant of the three queens, he falls among the common servants.

sentences.zh: 議者或云『今世等無奇才，不若取士於門』，此亦失矣。

translations.literal: Some who discuss the matter say, 'The present age equally lacks extraordinary talent; better to take scholars from eminent families'—this too is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that 'the present age lacks extraordinary talent, so it is better to take scholars from eminent families'—this too is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 豈可以世無周、邵，遂廢宰相邪！

translations.literal: Can one because the age lacks a Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao therefore abolish the office of chief minister!
translations.idiomatic: Can one because the age lacks a Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao abolish the office of chief minister!

sentences.zh: 但當校其寸長銖重者先敘之，則賢才無遺矣。

translations.literal: One need only compare each man's inch-long strengths and ounce-weight merits and promote them first—then no talent will be left behind.
translations.idiomatic: One need only rank men by whatever inch of merit they possess, and no talent will be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 又，刑罰之要，在於明當，不在於重。

translations.literal: Moreover, the essence of punishments lies in clarity and appropriateness, not in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the essence of punishment lies in clarity and appropriateness, not in severity.

sentences.zh: 苟不失有罪，雖捶撻之薄，人莫敢犯；

translations.literal: If the guilty are never missed, though the beating be light, none dare offend;
translations.idiomatic: If the guilty are never missed, though the beating be light, none dare offend;

sentences.zh: 若容可僥倖，雖參夷之嚴，不足懲禁。

translations.literal: if leniency allows escape by chance, though the punishment be as severe as tearing apart the body, it is not enough to warn and restrain.
translations.idiomatic: if leniency allows escape by chance, though the punishment tear the body apart, it will not restrain wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 今內外之官，欲邀當時之名，爭以深酷為無私，迭相敦厲，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: Now officials inside and outside the court, wishing to win a name in their time, vie to take deep severity as impartiality, urging one another on in turn, until it has become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials inside and outside the court, seeking reputation, vie to take harsh severity as impartiality, urging one another on until it has become custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下居九重之內，視人如赤子；

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells within the ninefold gates and views the people as infants;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells within the ninefold gates and views the people as infants;

sentences.zh: 百司分萬務之任，遇下如億讎。

translations.literal: the hundred offices share the burden of ten thousand affairs yet treat those below as a hundred million enemies.
translations.idiomatic: yet the hundred offices, sharing ten thousand affairs, treat those below as a hundred million enemies.

sentences.zh: 是則堯、舜止一人，而桀、紂以千百；

translations.literal: Thus Yao and Shun are but one man, while Jie and Zhou are a thousand or a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Thus there is but one Yao or Shun, while Jie and Zhou multiply by the thousand;

sentences.zh: 和氣不至，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: harmonious qi does not arrive—surely it is from this.
translations.idiomatic: and harmonious qi does not prevail—surely this is why.

sentences.zh: 謂宜敕示百僚，以惠元元之命。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that an edict should instruct the hundred officials, to show mercy to the lives of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Your Majesty should instruct the hundred officials to show mercy to the common people.

sentences.zh: 又，昔周居洛邑，猶存宗周；

translations.literal: Moreover, in former times when Zhou dwelt at Luoyi, it still preserved the ancestral Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Zhou dwelt at Luoyi, it still preserved the ancestral Zhou capital;

sentences.zh: 漢遷東都，京兆置尹。

translations.literal: when Han moved to the Eastern Capital, Jingzhao had a metropolitan magistrate appointed.
translations.idiomatic: when Han moved to the Eastern Capital, it appointed a metropolitan magistrate for Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 案《春秋》之義，有宗廟曰都，無曰邑。

translations.literal: According to the meaning of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, where there are ancestral temples it is called a capital; where there are none, a town.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, where there are ancestral temples it is called a capital; where there are none, a town.

sentences.zh: 況代京，宗廟山陵所托，王業所基，其為神鄉福地，實亦遠矣，今便同之郡國，臣竊不安。

translations.literal: How much more the capital of Dai, entrusted with the ancestral temples and imperial tombs, the foundation of the royal enterprise—its standing as sacred homeland and blessed land is truly far above the rest; to make it now the same as commanderies and states, your servant is privately uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: How much more the capital of Dai, entrusted with ancestral temples and imperial tombs, the foundation of the royal enterprise—its standing as sacred homeland is truly far above the rest; to reduce it now to the status of an ordinary commandery fills me with unease.

sentences.zh: 謂宜建畿置尹，一如故事，崇本重舊，光示萬葉。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that a metropolitan district should be established with a magistrate appointed, following the old precedent, honoring the root and valuing the past, to shine forth for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that a metropolitan district should be established with a magistrate appointed, following precedent, honoring the root and valuing the past, to shine forth for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 又，古者四民異居，欲其業專志定也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity the four classes dwelt apart, wishing their occupations to be specialized and their wills settled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity the four classes dwelt apart, so that each occupation might be specialized and each mind settled.

sentences.zh: 太祖道武皇帝創基撥亂，日不暇給，然猶分別士庶，不令雜居，工伎屠沽，各有攸處；

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu the High Ancestor, founding the realm and quelling disorder, had not a day to spare, yet still distinguished scholar and commoner, not permitting mixed residence; artisans, butchers, and traders each had their allotted places;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu the High Ancestor, founding the realm amid disorder, had not a day to spare, yet still distinguished scholars from commoners and forbade mixed residence; artisans, butchers, and traders each had their allotted quarters;

sentences.zh: 但不設科禁，久而混殽。

translations.literal: but because no statutory prohibitions were set, in time they became confused and mixed.
translations.idiomatic: but because no statutory prohibitions were set, in time the classes became confused.

sentences.zh: 今聞洛邑居民之制，專以官位相從，不分族類。

translations.literal: Now I hear that the regulations for residents of Luoyi rely solely on official rank for grouping, without distinguishing classes.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that regulations for Luoyang residents group people solely by official rank, without distinguishing class.

sentences.zh: 夫官位無常，朝榮夕悴，則是衣冠、皁隸不日同處矣。

translations.literal: Official rank is not constant—honored in the morning, wretched by evening—then gentry and black-clad servants would dwell together within days.
translations.idiomatic: Official rank is not constant—honored in the morning, ruined by evening—then gentry and commoners would dwell together within days.

sentences.zh: 借使一里之內，或調習歌舞，或講肄詩書，縱群兒隨其所之，則必不棄歌舞而從詩書矣。

translations.literal: Suppose that within a single lane, some practice song and dance while others study the Book of Songs and Documents; if children are left to go where they will, they will surely not abandon song and dance to follow the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose that within a single lane some practice song and dance while others study the classics; if children are left to go where they will, they will surely not abandon song and dance for the classics.

sentences.zh: 然則使工伎之家習士人風禮，百年難成；

translations.literal: Thus to make artisan households learn the manners of scholars would take a hundred years to accomplish;
translations.idiomatic: Thus to make artisan households learn scholarly manners would take a hundred years;

sentences.zh: 士人之子效工伎容態，一朝而就。

translations.literal: but for scholars' sons to imitate the bearing of artisans is done in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: but for scholars' sons to imitate artisans' ways is accomplished in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 是以仲尼稱裡仁之美，孟母勤三徙之訓。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius praised the beauty of benevolent neighbors, and Mencius's mother earnestly gave the lesson of three removals.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Confucius praised benevolent neighbors, and Mencius's mother gave the lesson of three removals.

sentences.zh: 此乃風俗之原，不可不察。

translations.literal: This is the root of custom and cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: This is the root of custom and cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每選人士，校其一婚一宦以為升降，何其密也！

translations.literal: The court, whenever it selects men, examines a single marriage and a single office for promotion or demotion—how meticulous!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court selects men, it examines a single marriage and a single office for promotion—how meticulous!

sentences.zh: 至於度地居民，則清濁連甍，何其略也！

translations.literal: Yet in allotting land and settling residents, pure and base are roof to roof—how careless!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in allotting land and settling residents, pure and base are roof to roof—how careless!

sentences.zh: 今因遷徙之初，皆是公地，分別工伎，在於一言，有何可疑，而闕盛美！

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the move, all is public land; to separate artisans requires but a word—what is there to doubt, that this splendid measure should be omitted!
translations.idiomatic: Now at the beginning of the move, all is public land; to separate artisans requires but a word—what is there to doubt, that this splendid measure should be omitted!

sentences.zh: 又，南人昔有淮北之地，自比中華，僑置郡縣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the southerners once held the lands north of the Huai, comparing themselves to the Central States and establishing expatriate commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the southerners once held the lands north of the Huai, comparing themselves to the Central States and establishing expatriate commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 自歸附聖化，仍而不改，名實交錯，文書難辨。

translations.literal: Since submitting to the sage transformation, they have remained unchanged; names and realities are crossed, and documents are hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Since submitting to the sage rule, they have remained unchanged; names and realities are crossed, and documents are hard to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 宜依地理舊名，一皆釐革，小者併合，大者分置，及中州郡縣，昔以戶少並省，今民口既多，亦可復舊。

translations.literal: They should follow the old geographical names and all be reformed; small ones merged, large ones divided and set up; and as for the central provinces' commanderies and counties, formerly merged for few households—now that the population is large, the old divisions may also be restored.
translations.idiomatic: They should follow old geographical names and all be reformed—small districts merged, large ones divided; and central provinces' commanderies and counties, formerly merged for few households, may now be restored as the population has grown.

sentences.zh: 又，君人者以天下為家，不可有所私。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who rules men takes all under Heaven as his household and may have nothing private.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a ruler takes all under Heaven as his household and may have nothing private.

sentences.zh: 倉庫之儲，以供軍國之用，自非有功德者不當加賜。

translations.literal: Stores in the granaries and treasuries are to supply the army and state; except for those with merit and virtue, none should receive added gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury stores are to supply the army and state; except for those with merit, none should receive added gifts.

sentences.zh: 在朝諸貴，受祿不輕；

translations.literal: The nobles at court receive salaries that are not light;
translations.idiomatic: The nobles at court already receive substantial salaries;

sentences.zh: 比來頒賚，動以千計。

translations.literal: of late the distributions and gifts have run to thousands at a time.
translations.idiomatic: yet of late distributions have run to thousands at a time.

sentences.zh: 若分以賜鰥寡孤獨之民，所濟實多；

translations.literal: If divided and given to widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary, the help would be truly great;
translations.idiomatic: If divided among widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary, the benefit would be far greater;

sentences.zh: 今直以與親近之臣，殆非『周急不继富』之謂也。」

translations.literal: now they are given directly to close ministers—this is scarcely the meaning of 'aid the urgent, do not add to the rich.'"
translations.idiomatic: yet now they are given directly to close ministers—this is scarcely the meaning of 'aid the urgent, do not add to the rich.'"

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，甚善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and greatly approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and greatly approved it.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，魏主如河陰，規方澤。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day yichou, the Wei sovereign went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the yichou day, the Wei emperor went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝祀明堂。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 司徒參軍劉學等聘於魏。

translations.literal: Liu Xue and others, staff officers of the Minister of Education, were sent on a mission to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xue and others, staff officers of the Minister of Education, were sent on a diplomatic mission to Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏徙河南王干為趙郡王，穎川王雍為高陽王。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Wei transferred Prince Gan of Henan to Prince of Zhao commandery and Prince Yong of Yingchuan to Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, Wei transferred Prince Gan of Henan to Prince of Zhao commandery and Prince Yong of Yingchuan to Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏主北巡；

translations.literal: On day renyin, the Wei sovereign toured north;
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, the Wei emperor toured north;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，濟河；

translations.literal: on day guimao, he crossed the river;
translations.idiomatic: on the guimao day, he crossed the river;

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，至平城。

translations.literal: in the third month, on day renshen, he reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: in the third month, on the renshen day, he reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 使群臣更論遷都利害，各言其志。

translations.literal: He had the ministers again debate the advantages and disadvantages of moving the capital, each stating his view.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ministers debate again the advantages and disadvantages of moving the capital, each stating his view.

sentences.zh: 燕州刺史穆羆曰：「今四方未定，未宜遷都。

translations.literal: Mu Pi, governor of Yan Province, said: "The four quarters are not yet settled; it is not yet fitting to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Pi, governor of Yan Province, said, "The four quarters are not yet settled; it is not yet fitting to move the capital.

sentences.zh: 且征伐無馬，將何以克？」

translations.literal: Moreover, in campaigns there are no horses—how will we conquer?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in campaigns there are no horses—how will we conquer?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「廄牧在代，何患無馬！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The stud farms are at Dai—why fear there are no horses!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The stud farms are at Dai—why fear there are no horses!

sentences.zh: 今代在恆山之北，九州之外，非帝王之都也。」

translations.literal: Now Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces—it is not a capital for emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces—it is not a capital fit for emperors."

sentences.zh: 尚書於果曰：「臣非以代地為勝伊、洛之美也。

translations.literal: Yu Guo, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, said: "Your servant does not hold that the land of Dai surpasses the beauty of Yi and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guo, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, said, "I do not hold that Dai surpasses the beauty of Yi and Luo.

sentences.zh: 但自先帝以來，久居於此，百姓安之；

translations.literal: But since the former emperors, we have long dwelt here and the people are settled;
translations.idiomatic: But since the former emperors we have long dwelt here and the people are settled;

sentences.zh: 一旦南遷，眾情不樂。」

translations.literal: if we move south in a single day, the multitude will not be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: if we move south in a single day, the people will not be pleased."

sentences.zh: 平陽公丕曰：「遷都大事，當迅之卜筮。」

translations.literal: Prince Pi of Pingyang said: "The great affair of moving the capital should be swiftly submitted to divination."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pi of Pingyang said, "The great affair of moving the capital should be swiftly submitted to divination."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔周、邵聖賢，乃能卜宅。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In former times the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were sages and could divine a dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In former times the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were sages and could divine a dwelling.

sentences.zh: 今無其人，卜之何益！

translations.literal: Now there is no such man—what use is divination!
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no such man—what use is divination!

sentences.zh: 且卜以決疑，不疑何卜！

translations.literal: Moreover, one divines to resolve doubt—when there is no doubt, why divine!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one divines to resolve doubt—when there is no doubt, why divine!

sentences.zh: 黃帝卜而龜焦，天老曰『吉』，黃帝從之。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor divined and the tortoise shell was scorched; the Heavenly Elder said 'auspicious,' and the Yellow Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor divined and the tortoise shell was scorched; the Heavenly Elder said 'auspicious,' and the Yellow Emperor followed him.

sentences.zh: 然則至人之知未然，審於龜矣。

translations.literal: Thus the utmost man's knowledge of what is not yet manifest is more certain than the tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the utmost man's foreknowledge is more certain than the tortoise.

sentences.zh: 王者以四海為家，或南或北，何常之有！

translations.literal: A king takes the four seas as his household—south or north, what constancy is there!
translations.idiomatic: A king takes the four seas as his household—south or north, what constancy is there!

sentences.zh: 朕之遠祖，世居北荒，平文皇帝始都東木根山，昭成皇帝更營盛樂，道武皇帝遷於平城。

translations.literal: My remote ancestors dwelt generation after generation in the northern wilds; Emperor Pingwen first made his capital at Eastern Mugen Mountain, Emperor Zhaocheng rebuilt at Shengle, and Emperor Daowu moved to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: My remote ancestors dwelt generation after generation in the northern wilds; Emperor Pingwen first made his capital at Eastern Mugen Mountain, Emperor Zhaocheng rebuilt at Shengle, and Emperor Daowu moved to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 朕幸屬勝殘之運，何為獨不得遷乎！」

translations.literal: I have fortunately inherited an age that conquers the cruel—why alone may I not move!
translations.idiomatic: I have fortunately inherited an age that conquers cruelty—why alone may I not move!"

sentences.zh: 群臣不敢復言。

translations.literal: The ministers dared speak no further.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers dared speak no further.

sentences.zh: 羆，壽之孫；

translations.literal: Pi was the grandson of Shou;
translations.idiomatic: Pi was the grandson of Shou;

sentences.zh: 果，烈之弟也。

translations.literal: Guo was the younger brother of Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was the younger brother of Lie.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏主臨朝堂，部分遷留。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, the Wei sovereign attended court in the hall and assigned who would move and who would remain.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, the Wei emperor attended court and assigned who would move and who would remain.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，魏罷西郊祭天。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day gengchen, Wei abolished the western suburb sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the gengchen day, Wei abolished the western suburb sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，武陵昭王曄卒。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, Xiao Ye, Illustrious Prince of Wuling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, Xiao Ye, Illustrious Prince of Wuling, died.

sentences.zh: 戊子，竟陵文宣王子良以憂卒。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Xiao Ziliang, Cultured and Illustrious Prince of Jingling, died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day, Xiao Ziliang, Cultured and Illustrious Prince of Jingling, died of grief.

sentences.zh: 帝常憂子良為變，聞其卒，甚喜。

translations.literal: The emperor had constantly feared Ziliang would rebel; hearing of his death, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had constantly feared Ziliang would rebel; hearing of his death, he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：孔子稱「鄙夫不可與事君，未得之，患得之；

translations.literal: Minister Guang says: Confucius said, "The base fellow cannot be entrusted with serving a ruler; before obtaining it, he worries he will not obtain it;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Confucius said, "A vulgar man is unfit to serve his sovereign; before he gains office, he fears he will not gain it;

sentences.zh: 既得之，患失之。

translations.literal: Once he has obtained it, he worries he will lose it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he holds it, he fears he will lose it.

sentences.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至。」

translations.literal: If he worries about losing it, there is nothing to which he will not go."
translations.idiomatic: If he dreads losing what he has, there is no limit to what he will do."

sentences.zh: 王融乘危徼幸，謀易嗣君。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, riding peril to seek fortune, plotted to change the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong seized a moment of crisis to gamble for advantage and schemed to replace the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子良當時賢王，雖素以忠慎自居，不免憂死。

translations.literal: Ziliang was the worthy prince of the time; though he had always taken loyalty and caution as his stand, he could not escape dying of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was the most admired prince of his day; though he had always prided himself on loyalty and prudence, he still died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 跡其所以然，正由融速求富貴而已。

translations.literal: Tracing why this came about, it was simply because Rong was hastening to seek wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Trace the cause to its root, and it was nothing more than Rong's rush to seize wealth and status.

sentences.zh: 輕躁之士，烏可近哉！

translations.literal: A frivolous and impetuous fellow— how can one draw near to him!
translations.idiomatic: How can anyone keep company with a man so rash and unstable!

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏罷五月五日、七月七日饗祖考。

translations.literal: On day jihai, Wei abolished the fifth day of the fifth month and seventh day of the seventh month sacrifices to ancestors and forefathers.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day, Wei discontinued the ancestral offerings held on the fifth day of the fifth month and the seventh day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 魏錄尚書事廣陵王羽奏：「令文：每歲終，州鎮列屬官治狀，及再考，則行黜陟。

translations.literal: Wei Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing Guangyang Prince Yu memorialized: "The ordinance text: At each year's end, provinces and garrisons list subordinate officials' conduct records, and at the second review demotions and promotions are carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Guangyang, who recorded affairs for the Masters of Writing in Wei, memorialized: "The statute provides that at year's end each province and garrison shall report on its subordinates' performance, and after a second review promotions and dismissals shall follow.

sentences.zh: 去十五年京官盡經考為三等，今已三載。

translations.literal: Fifteen years ago capital officials all underwent review as third grade; it has now been three years.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years have passed since all capital officials were last rated in the third review cycle, and three years have elapsed since then.

sentences.zh: 臣輒准外考，以定京官治行。」

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to apply the external review standard to fix capital officials' conduct ratings."
translations.idiomatic: I propose applying the provincial review procedure now to determine the capital officials' performance grades."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「考績事重，應關朕聽，不可輕發；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said: "Performance review is weighty; it should concern my hearing; it cannot be lightly initiated;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor replied: "Merit review is a grave matter that should come before me; it must not be launched lightly;

sentences.zh: 且俟至秋。」

translations.literal: Wait until autumn."
translations.idiomatic: Let it wait until autumn."

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁卯，鎮軍將軍鸞即本號，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, dingmao, General Who Guards the Army Luan assumed his original title with establishment of an office equal to the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the dingmao day, Luan, General Who Guards the Army, retained his existing rank and was granted an establishment equal to the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以新安王昭文為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was made governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was appointed governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 五月，申戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day shenxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the cycle (shenxu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六月，己巳，魏遣兼員外散騎常侍盧昶、兼員外散騎侍郎王清石為聘。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jisi, Wei sent concurrent Supernumerary Master of Writing on the Left of the Imperial Carriage Lu Chang and concurrent Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Carriage Wang Qingshi as envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jisi day, Wei dispatched Lu Chang, concurrent supernumerary master of writing on the left of the imperial carriage, and Wang Qingshi, concurrent supernumerary gentleman attendant at the imperial carriage, as envoys on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 昶，度世之子也。

translations.literal: Chang was the son of Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was a son of Dushi.

sentences.zh: 清石世仕江南，魏主謂清石曰：「卿勿以南人自嫌。

translations.literal: Qingshi's family had served in Jiangnan for generations; the Wei emperor said to Qingshi: "Do not look down on yourself for being a southerner.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshi's family had long served in the south; the Wei emperor told him: "Do not belittle yourself for being a man of the south.

sentences.zh: 彼有知識，欲見則見，欲言則言。

translations.literal: If people there have acquaintanceship with you, if you wish to see them then see them; if you wish to speak then speak.
translations.idiomatic: If you have friends there, visit whom you wish and say what you wish.

sentences.zh: 凡使人以和為貴，勿迭相矜誇，見於辭色，失將命之體也。」

translations.literal: In general when sending envoys, harmony is prized; do not take turns boasting to each other, displaying it in words and expression— that loses the proper bearing of bearing the sovereign's charge."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys above all must value harmony; do not trade boasts or let rivalry show in speech and manner, for that betrays the dignity of an imperial mission."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙亥，魏以宋王劉昶為使持節、都督吳、越、楚諸軍事、大將軍，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, yihai, Wei made Liu Chang, Prince of Song, commissioner holding credentials with full authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Wu, Yue, and Chu, Grand General, stationed at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the yihai day, Wei appointed Liu Chang, Prince of Song, as commissioner with full powers, commander of all forces in Wu, Yue, and Chu, and Grand General, with his headquarters at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏主親餞之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor personally saw him off with a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor personally gave him a farewell banquet.

sentences.zh: 以王肅為昶府長史。

translations.literal: Wang Su was made chief administrator of Chang's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was appointed chief administrator of Chang's staff.

sentences.zh: 昶至鎮，不能撫接義故，卒無成功。

translations.literal: Chang reached his post but could not comfort and win over his old associates; in the end he achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang took up his command, he failed to rally his former comrades, and in the end accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏安定靖王休卒。

translations.literal: On day renwu, Wei Prince Jing of Anding Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Xiu, Prince Jing of Anding in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 自卒至殯，魏主三臨其第；

translations.literal: From death to encoffinement, the Wei emperor three times visited his residence;
translations.idiomatic: From his death until the laying in the coffin, the Wei emperor visited his house three times;

sentences.zh: 葬之如尉元之禮，送之出郊，慟哭而返。

translations.literal: Buried him with the rites accorded Yu Yuan; escorted him beyond the suburbs, wept bitterly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He buried him with the honors given Yu Yuan, escorted the coffin beyond the city, and returned weeping.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏主北巡。

translations.literal: On day renxu, the Wei emperor toured the north.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, the Wei emperor made a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞既誅徐龍駒、周奉叔，而尼媼外入者，頗傳異語。

translations.literal: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had executed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women entering from outside rather widely spread strange talk.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had killed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women coming in from outside spread all manner of alarming rumors.

sentences.zh: 中書令何胤，以後之從叔，為帝所親，使直殿省。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Yin, being a paternal uncle on the empress's side, was intimate with the emperor and was made to attend the Hall Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin, Director of the Secretariat, was a maternal uncle of the empress and a favorite of the emperor, who had him serve in the Hall Directorate.

sentences.zh: 帝與胤謀誅鸞，令胤受事；

translations.literal: The emperor with Yin plotted to kill Luan and ordered Yin to take charge of the matter;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor plotted with Yin to kill Luan and told Yin to take charge;

sentences.zh: 胤不敢當，依違諫說，帝意復止。

translations.literal: Yin did not dare undertake it, vacillating with admonitory persuasion, and the emperor's intent again ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not dare accept the role; he hedged and urged caution, and the emperor's resolve faded again.

sentences.zh: 乃謀出鸞於西州，中敕用事，不復關咨於鸞。

translations.literal: Then they plotted to send Luan out to Western Province; central edicts would govern affairs, no longer consulting Luan.
translations.idiomatic: They then planned to post Luan away to Western Province so that central orders would govern affairs without consulting him.

sentences.zh: 是時，蕭諶、蕭坦之握兵權，左僕射王晏總尚書事。

translations.literal: At this time Chen and Tanzhi held military authority; Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan oversaw Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Chen and Tanzhi controlled the army, while Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, oversaw the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 諶密召諸王典簽，約語之，不許諸王外接人物。

translations.literal: Chen secretly summoned the palace stewards of the princes, made agreements with them, not permitting the princes to receive people from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Chen secretly summoned each prince's chief clerk, bound them by agreement, and forbade the princes to receive outsiders.

sentences.zh: 諶親要日久，眾皆憚而從之。

translations.literal: Chen had been intimate and influential for many days; all feared him and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had long been close to power, and everyone feared him and complied.

sentences.zh: 鸞以其謀告王晏，晏聞之，響應；

translations.literal: Luan reported his plot to Wang Yan; Yan on hearing it responded in agreement;
translations.idiomatic: Luan disclosed his plan to Wang Yan, who at once assented;

sentences.zh: 又告丹陽尹徐孝嗣，孝嗣亦從之。

translations.literal: He also told Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang; Xiaosi also followed.
translations.idiomatic: He also informed Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang, and Xiaosi went along as well.

sentences.zh: 驃騎錄事南陽樂豫謂孝嗣曰：「外傳籍籍，似有伊、周之事。

translations.literal: Recorder of Affairs under the Rapid Cavalry General Leyu of Nanyang said to Xiaosi: "Outside the talk is widespread, as if there were an Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou affair.
translations.idiomatic: Leyu of Nanyang, recorder on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General, told Xiaosi: "Rumors are everywhere, as though someone were playing Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou to the throne.

sentences.zh: 君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷托附之重，恐不得同人此舉。

translations.literal: You received Emperor Wu's exceptional grace, bore the weight of entrustment— I fear you cannot go along with this action in common with them.
translations.idiomatic: You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bore a heavy trust; I fear you cannot join them in this.

sentences.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。」

translations.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu; to this day teeth are cold."
translations.idiomatic: Men still mock Lord Chu, and the mockery has not grown stale."

sentences.zh: 孝嗣心然之，而不能從。

translations.literal: Xiaosi inwardly agreed but could not refuse to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi agreed in his heart but could not bring himself to refuse.

sentences.zh: 帝謂蕭坦之曰：「人言鎮軍與王晏、蕭諶欲共廢我，似非虛傳。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army with Wang Yan and Xiao Chen together wish to depose me— it does not seem a false rumor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army, Wang Yan, and Chen are plotting to depose me together. That does not sound like idle talk.

sentences.zh: 卿所聞雲何？」

translations.literal: What have you heard?"
translations.idiomatic: What have you heard on your side?"

sentences.zh: 坦之曰：「天下寧當有此，誰樂無事廢天子邪！

translations.literal: Tanzhi said: "Would such a thing really exist under Heaven— who would delight in deposing the Son of Heaven when there is nothing wrong!
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi replied: "Could such a thing truly happen in the world? Who would want to depose the Son of Heaven when nothing is amiss!

sentences.zh: 朝貴不容造此論，當是諸尼姥言耳，豈有信邪！

translations.literal: Court nobles would not allow such talk to be made; it must be the words of those nuns and old women— how could there be belief!
translations.idiomatic: The great officials of court would never invent such talk; it must be those nuns and old women. How could anyone believe it!

sentences.zh: 官若無事除此二人，誰敢自保！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty without cause removed these two men, who would dare protect himself!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty removed these two men without cause, who would dare think himself safe!"

sentences.zh: 直閣將軍曹道剛疑外間有異，密有處分，謀未能發。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Gate Cao Daogang suspected something unusual outside, had secret dispositions, but the plot could not be launched.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Daogang, Director of the Palace Gate, suspected trouble outside and made secret arrangements, but the plot never came off.

sentences.zh: 時始興內史蕭季敞、南陽太守蕭穎基皆內遷，諶欲待二人至，藉其勢力以舉事。

translations.literal: At this time the interior governor of Shixing Xiao Jichang and governor of Nanyang Xiao Yingji were both transferred inward; Chen wished to wait until the two arrived to rely on their power to raise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Jichang, interior governor of Shixing, and Xiao Yingji, governor of Nanyang, were both being recalled to the capital; Chen wanted to wait for them and use their strength to launch the coup.

sentences.zh: 鸞慮事變，以告坦之，坦之馳謂諶曰：「廢天子，古來大事。

translations.literal: Luan feared matters would change, told Tanzhi; Tanzhi galloped to tell Chen: "Deposing the Son of Heaven is a great matter of old.
translations.idiomatic: Luan feared the moment would slip away and told Tanzhi, who rode at once to Chen and said: "Deposing the Son of Heaven has always been a grave undertaking.

sentences.zh: 比聞曹道剛、朱隆之等轉已猜疑，衛尉明日若不就事，無所復及。

translations.literal: Recently heard Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi and others are increasingly suspicious; if the Commandant of the Guard does not act tomorrow, nothing more can be done.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi, and the rest are growing suspicious. If the Commandant of the Guard does not move tomorrow, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 弟有百歲母，豈能坐聽禍敗，正應作餘計耳！」

translations.literal: Younger brother, you have a mother of a hundred years— can you sit and listen to ruin and defeat come? You should make other plans!"
translations.idiomatic: You have a mother nearing a hundred— can you sit still while disaster closes in? You must act now!"

sentences.zh: 諶惶遽從之。

translations.literal: Chen in panic hastily followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, alarmed, agreed at once.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，鸞使蕭諶先入宮，遇曹道剛及中書舍人朱隆之，皆殺之。

translations.literal: On day renchen, Luan sent Chen to enter the palace first; encountering Cao Daogang and Master of Writing Attendant Zhu Longzhi, he killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, Luan sent Chen into the palace ahead of him; Chen met Cao Daogang and Zhu Longzhi, Master of Writing Attendant, and killed them both.

sentences.zh: 直後徐僧亮盛怒，大言於眾曰：「吾等荷恩，今日應死報！」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xu Sengliang was greatly enraged and spoke loudly before the crowd: "We have received grace; today we should repay with death!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sengliang, palace attendant, flew into a rage and cried out to those around him: "We owe the emperor our lives; today we must repay him with death!"

sentences.zh: 又殺之。

translations.literal: He was killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed.

sentences.zh: 鸞引兵自尚書入雲龍門，戎服加朱衣於上，比入門，三失履。

translations.literal: Luan led troops from the Masters of Writing into the Cloud Dragon Gate, military dress with vermilion robe over it; by the time he entered the gate he had lost his shoes three times.
translations.idiomatic: Luan led his troops from the Masters of Writing compound through the Cloud Dragon Gate, wearing armor with a vermilion robe over it; before he crossed the threshold he lost his shoes three times.

sentences.zh: 王晏、徐孝嗣、蕭坦之、陳顯達、王廣之、沈文季皆隨其後。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed in his train.

sentences.zh: 帝在壽昌殿。

translations.literal: The emperor was in the Shouchang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the Hall of Longevity and Prosperity.

sentences.zh: 聞外有變，猶密為手敕呼蕭諶，又使閉內殿諸房閣。

translations.literal: Hearing there was disturbance outside, he still secretly made a hand edict summoning Chen, and also ordered the inner hall rooms and pavilions closed.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard trouble outside, he still secretly drafted a personal order summoning Chen and had the inner chambers and side halls barred.

sentences.zh: 俄而諶引兵入壽昌閣，帝走趨徐姬房，拔劍自刺，不入，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。

translations.literal: Before long Chen led troops into the Shouchang Pavilion; the emperor ran to Lady Xu's quarters, drew his sword to stab himself but did not penetrate, wrapped his neck in silk, and was carried out by litter to the Yande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen marched into the Shouchang Pavilion. The emperor fled to Lady Xu's rooms, tried to stab himself but failed, bound his neck in silk, and was carried out on a litter to the Hall of Extended Virtue.

sentences.zh: 諶初入殿，宿衛將士皆操弓楯欲拒戰。

translations.literal: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards all grasped bows and shields wishing to resist and fight.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards seized bows and shields, ready to fight.

sentences.zh: 諶謂之曰：「所取自有人，卿等不須動！」

translations.literal: Chen said to them: "The one taken has his own person; you need not move!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen told them: "We are only taking the man we came for; none of you need stir!"

sentences.zh: 宿衛素隸服於諶，皆信之，及見帝出，各欲自奮，帝竟無一言。

translations.literal: The palace guards had long been subordinate to Chen and all believed him; when they saw the emperor brought out, each wished to exert himself, but the emperor in the end said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: The guards had long served under Chen and trusted him. When they saw the emperor led away, several wanted to fight, but the emperor never spoke a word.

sentences.zh: 行至西弄，弒之。

translations.literal: When they reached the western lane, they assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the western passage they murdered him.

sentences.zh: 輿屍出殯徐龍駒宅，葬以王禮。

translations.literal: They carried the corpse out and encoffined it at Xu Longju's residence, burying him with princely rites.
translations.idiomatic: They carried his body out and laid it in state at Xu Longju's house, then buried him with the honors due a prince.

sentences.zh: 徐姬及諸嬖倖皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Lady Xu and all the favored minions were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu and all the emperor's favorites were put to death.

sentences.zh: 鸞既執帝，欲作太后令；

translations.literal: After Luan had seized the emperor, he wished to draft an empress dowager order;
translations.idiomatic: Once Luan held the emperor captive, he wanted to issue an order in the empress dowager's name;

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣於袖中出而進之，鸞大悅。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi produced it from his sleeve and presented it; Luan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi drew the draft from his sleeve and submitted it, and Luan was delighted.
