sentences.zh: 癸巳，以太后令追廢帝為鬱林王，又廢何後為王妃，迎立新安王昭文。

translations.literal: On day guisi, by empress dowager order the emperor was posthumously deposed as Prince of Yulin, Empress He was also deposed as princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was welcomed and established.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day, by order of the empress dowager the emperor was posthumously demoted to Prince of Yulin, Empress He was reduced to princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was installed on the throne.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書謝瀹方與客圍棋，左右聞有變，驚走報瀹。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xie Yue was just playing go with a guest; attendants on hearing there was disturbance startled and ran to report to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yue, Minister of Personnel, was playing go with a guest when his attendants heard of the upheaval, rushed in alarm, and told him.

sentences.zh: 瀹每下子，輒云「其當有意」，竟局，乃還齋臥，竟不問外事。

translations.literal: With each move Yue placed a stone he would say "there must be intent in this"; when the game ended he returned to his study to lie down and in the end did not ask about outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With every stone he played, Yue murmured, "They must have their reasons." When the game ended he went back to his quarters to sleep and never asked what had happened outside.

sentences.zh: 大匠卿虞悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛褲廢天子，天下豈有此理邪！」

translations.literal: Master of Works Yu Song secretly sighed: "Wang and Xu have thus trussed their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven— under Heaven can there be such a principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song, Master of Works, muttered to himself: "Wang and Xu have tied up their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven. Can such a thing exist in the world!"

sentences.zh: 悰，嘯父之孫也。

translations.literal: Song was the grandson of Xiaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Song was a grandson of Xiaofu.

sentences.zh: 朝臣被召入宮。

translations.literal: Court ministers were summoned to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials were summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒江學至雲龍門，托藥發，吐車中而去。

translations.literal: Libationer of the National University Jiang Xue reached the Cloud Dragon Gate, pleaded illness onset, vomited in the carriage and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xue, libationer of the National University, reached the Cloud Dragon Gate, claimed a sudden illness, vomited in his carriage, and went home.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯鸞欲引中散大夫孫謙為腹心，使兼衛尉給甲仗百人。

translations.literal: Luan, Marquis of Xichang, wished to draw in Palace Attendant Sun Qian as his intimate and had him concurrently serve as Commandant of the Guard, supplying armor and weapons to a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, Marquis of Xichang, wanted Sun Qian, palace attendant, as his confidant and made him act as Commandant of the Guard with a hundred armed men.

sentences.zh: 謙不欲與之同，輒散甲士；

translations.literal: Qian did not wish to be of one mind with him and promptly dispersed the armored soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Qian refused to go along and immediately dismissed the armed men;

sentences.zh: 鸞亦不之罪也。

translations.literal: Luan also did not punish him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，新安王即皇帝位，時年十五。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, assumed the imperial position; he was fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day, Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, ascended the throne at the age of fifteen.

sentences.zh: 以西昌侯鸞為驃騎大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州刺史、宣城郡公。

translations.literal: Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was made Rapid Cavalry General, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, governor of Yang Province, and Duke of Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was appointed Rapid Cavalry General, recorder of affairs for the Masters of Writing, governor of Yang Province, and Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元延興。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed; the era name was changed to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared, and the reign era was changed to Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏主至朔州。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, the Wei emperor reached Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, the Wei emperor arrived at Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，以司空王敬則為太尉。

translations.literal: Eighth month, jiachen, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the jiachen day, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王鏘為司徒，車騎大將軍陳顯達為司空，尚書左僕射王晏為尚書令。

translations.literal: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, was made Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Minister of Works; Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, became Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, became Minister of Works; and Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏主至陰山。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 以始安王遙光為南郡太守，不之官。

translations.literal: Shi'an Prince Yaoguang was made governor of Nan commandery but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang, Prince of Shi'an, was named governor of Nan commandery but never went to his post.

sentences.zh: 遙光，鸞之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yaoguang was Luan's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang was a nephew of Luan.

sentences.zh: 鸞有異志，遙光贊成之，凡大誅賞，無不預謀。

translations.literal: Luan had a different intent; Yaoguang assisted and accomplished it; in every great execution or reward, none was without his prior plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Luan harbored larger ambitions, and Yaoguang backed him; every major punishment or reward was plotted with his help.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以中書郎蕭遙欣為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Palace Attendant Xiao Yaoxin was made governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Yaoxin, palace attendant, was appointed governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 遙欣，遙光之弟也。

translations.literal: Yaoxin was Yaoguang's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxin was Yaoguang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 鸞欲樹置親黨，故用之。

translations.literal: Luan wished to plant and establish his own faction, therefore he employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Luan wanted to place his own kin in power, and so he used them.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏主如懷朔鎮；

translations.literal: On day guichou, the Wei emperor went to Huaishuo Garrison;
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day, the Wei emperor went to Huaishuo Garrison;

sentences.zh: 己未，如武川鎮；

translations.literal: On day jiwei, he went to Wuchuan Garrison;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day, he went to Wuchuan Garrison;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，如撫宜鎮；

translations.literal: On day xinyou, he went to Fuyi Garrison;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, he went to Fuyi Garrison;

sentences.zh: 甲子，如柔玄鎮；

translations.literal: On day jiazi, he went to Rouxuan Garrison;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, he went to Rouxuan Garrison;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，南還；

translations.literal: On day yichou, he returned south;
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, he turned back south;

sentences.zh: 辛未，至平城。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he arrived at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day, the Wei emperor reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬申朔，魏詔曰：「三載考績，三考黜陟；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the new-moon day renren, the Wei issued an edict saying: "After three years examine achievements; after three examinations demote and promote;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renren new moon, the Northern Wei court proclaimed: "The ancient rule assesses a man's record every three years and promotes or dismisses him only after three such reviews;

sentences.zh: 可黜者不足為遲，可進者大成賒緩。

translations.literal: Those who may be demoted are not considered too late; those who may be advanced find great achievement greatly deferred and slow.
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to be removed linger in office too long, while those who deserve reward wait endlessly for it.

sentences.zh: 朕今三載一考，即行黜陟，欲令愚滯無妨於賢者，才能不擁於下位。

translations.literal: I now with one examination every three years immediately carry out demotion and promotion, wishing to make the stupid and stagnant not obstruct the worthy, and ability not congested in low positions.
translations.idiomatic: I shall now hold an assessment every three years and act on it at once, so that the dull and idle cannot block the capable and talent will not be bottled up in subordinate ranks.

sentences.zh: 各令當曹考其優劣為三等，其上下二等仍分為三。

translations.literal: Each shall order the relevant bureau to examine their superiority and inferiority into three grades; the upper and lower two grades again are divided into three.
translations.idiomatic: Let each department grade its officers' merit in three tiers, and subdivide the top and bottom tiers each into three ranks.

sentences.zh: 六品已下，尚書重問；

translations.literal: For sixth rank and below, the Ministry Director shall re-examine;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the sixth rank and lower shall undergo a further review by the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 五品已上，朕將親與公卿論其善惡，上上者遷之，下下者黜之，中者守其本任。」

translations.literal: For fifth rank and above, I shall personally with the dukes and ministers discuss their good and evil; the top-top shall be transferred, the bottom-bottom demoted, the middle keep their original post."
translations.idiomatic: for the fifth rank and above, I shall personally deliberate with the nobles and ministers on each man's conduct—the highest of the high will be advanced, the lowest of the low dismissed, and the middling left in their present posts."

sentences.zh: 魏主之北巡也。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler toured north.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's northern tour,

sentences.zh: 留任城王澄銓簡舊臣。

translations.literal: He left Prince of Ren-cheng Cheng to examine and select old officials.
translations.idiomatic: he had left Prince Ren of Pingcheng to evaluate the veteran officials.

sentences.zh: 自公侯已下，有官者以萬數，澄品其優劣能否為三等，人無怨者。

translations.literal: From dukes and marquises downward, those with posts numbered in the tens of thousands; Cheng graded their superiority, inferiority, ability, and incapacity into three ranks, and no one complained.
translations.idiomatic: From the highest nobles down, there were tens of thousands of officeholders; Cheng rated them in three tiers by merit and competence, and none raised a grievance.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏主臨朝堂，黜陟百官，謂諸尚書曰：「尚書，樞機之任，非徒總虛務，行文書而已；

translations.literal: On renwu, the Wei ruler attended the court hall, demoting and promoting the hundred officials, saying to the various Directors of Ministries: "The Ministry Director bears the pivot-and-key responsibility, not merely summing empty affairs and issuing documents only;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the emperor presided in the main hall to promote and dismiss the bureaucracy. Addressing the ministers, he said: "The heads of the ministries hold the pivot of state—your charge is not merely to tally paperwork and circulate memorials;

sentences.zh: 朕之得失，盡在於此。

translations.literal: My gains and losses all lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: My successes and failures as ruler depend entirely upon you.

sentences.zh: 卿等居官，年垂再期，未嘗獻可替否，進一賢退一不肖，此最罪之大者。」

translations.literal: You hold office, years nearly reaching two terms, never once offered approval and rejection, advancing one worthy and retiring one unworthy—this is the greatest of crimes."
translations.idiomatic: You have served nearly two full terms without once recommending a worthy man or removing an unworthy one; that is your gravest fault."

sentences.zh: 又謂錄尚書事廣陵王羽曰：「汝為朕弟，居機衡之右，無勤恪之聲，有阿黨之跡。

translations.literal: Again he said to Recorder of Ministry Affairs Prince of Guangling Yu: "You are my younger brother, dwelling to the right of the pivot-scale, without sound of diligence and reverence, having traces of partisan cliques.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Prince Guangling Yu, who held the registry of memorials: "You are my own brother, seated at the heart of government, yet you have shown neither industry nor integrity, only signs of faction.

sentences.zh: 今黜汝錄尚書、廷尉，但為特進、太子太保。」

translations.literal: Now I demote you from Recorder of Ministry Affairs and Commandant of Justice, only making you specially advanced and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: I strip you of the registry and the Court of Justice, leaving you only as Specially Advanced and Grand Mentor to the Heir."

sentences.zh: 又謖尚書令陸睿曰：「叔翻到省之初，甚有善稱；

translations.literal: Again he rebuked Director of Ministries Lu Rui, saying: "When Uncle Fan first came to the ministry, he had much good reputation;
translations.idiomatic: He next rebuked Lu Rui, Minister of the Left: "When Uncle Fan first took up his post, his reputation was excellent;

sentences.zh: 比來偏頗懈怠，由卿不能相導以義。

translations.literal: Recently he has been partial and slack, because you could not guide each other with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: of late he has grown biased and lax, and that is because you failed to guide him in what is right.

sentences.zh: 雖無大責，宜有小罰，今奪卿祿一期。」

translations.literal: Although without great blame, there should be a small punishment; now I strip your salary for one term."
translations.idiomatic: You are not guilty of a capital offense, but you deserve a lesser penalty: I withhold your salary for one review period."

sentences.zh: 又謂左僕射拓跋贊曰：「叔翻受黜，卿應大辟；

translations.literal: Again he said to Left Vice Director Tuoba Zan: "Uncle Fan received demotion; you ought to receive the death penalty;
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the Left Vice Director Tuoba Zan, he said: "Uncle Fan has been punished; by rights you should face execution;

sentences.zh: 但以咎歸一人，不復重責；

translations.literal: But because guilt returns to one person, I do not again heavily punish;
translations.idiomatic: but I lay the blame on a single man and will not punish you twice.

sentences.zh: 今解卿少師，削祿一期。」

translations.literal: Now I relieve you of Junior Mentor and cut your salary for one term."
translations.idiomatic: I relieve you of your post as Junior Mentor and cut your salary for one term."

sentences.zh: 又謂左丞公孫良、右丞乞伏義受曰：「卿亦應大辟；

translations.literal: Again he said to Left Assistant Gongsun Liang and Right Assistant Qifu Yishou: "You also ought to receive the death penalty;
translations.idiomatic: To the Left and Right Assistants Gongsun Liang and Qifu Yishou he said: "You too deserve execution;

sentences.zh: 可以白衣守本官，冠服祿恤盡從削奪。

translations.literal: You may in plain clothes keep your original post; crown, garments, salary, and stipends all follow stripping.
translations.idiomatic: you may remain in your posts as commoners in plain dress, stripped of rank, salary, and perquisites.

sentences.zh: 若三年有成，還復本任；

translations.literal: If within three years there is achievement, return and restore the original post;
translations.idiomatic: If within three years you prove yourselves, you may be restored;

sentences.zh: 無成，永歸南畝。」

translations.literal: Without achievement, forever return to the south fields."
translations.idiomatic: if not, you will till the southern fields forever."

sentences.zh: 又謂尚書任城王澄曰：「叔神志驕傲，可解少保。」

translations.literal: Again he said to Director Ren-cheng Wang Cheng: "Uncle Zhi's spirit is arrogant; he may be relieved of Junior Guardian."
translations.idiomatic: To the Director Wang Cheng of Ren he said: "Uncle Zhi has grown insufferably proud; relieve him of the Junior Guardianship."

sentences.zh: 又謂長兼尚書於果曰：「卿不勤職事，數辭以疾。

translations.literal: Again he said to Senior Acting Director Yu Guo: "You do not diligently perform your duties, repeatedly excusing yourself citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: To the acting senior director Yu Guo he said: "You neglect your duties and repeatedly plead illness.

sentences.zh: 可解長兼，削祿一期。」

translations.literal: You may be relieved of the senior acting post and have your salary cut for one term."
translations.idiomatic: Relieve him of his acting senior post and cut his salary for one term."

sentences.zh: 其餘守尚書尉羽、盧淵等，並以不職，或解任，或黜官，或奪祿，皆面數其過而行之。

translations.literal: The rest—acting Directors Wei Yu, Lu Yuan, and others—all for not performing duties, some relieved of post, some demoted in office, some stripped of salary; all had their faults enumerated to their faces and then were acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining acting directors—Wei Yu, Lu Yuan, and the rest—were likewise dismissed, demoted, or stripped of salary for dereliction; the emperor recited each man's faults to his face before pronouncing sentence.

sentences.zh: 淵，昶之兄也。

translations.literal: Yuan was Chang's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan was the elder brother of Lu Chang.

sentences.zh: 帝又謂陸睿曰：「北人每言『北俗質魯，何由知書！』

translations.literal: The Emperor again said to Lu Rui: "Northerners often say, 'Northern customs are crude and dull—how could they know books!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke again to Lu Rui: "Northerners constantly say, 'Our northern ways are rustic—how could we know the classics!' Whenever I hear that, it grieves me deeply!

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，深用憮然！

translations.literal: When I hear this, I am deeply disheartened!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I hear that, it grieves me deeply!

sentences.zh: 今知書者甚眾，豈皆聖人！

translations.literal: Now those who know books are very many—are they all sages!
translations.idiomatic: Today many northerners are literate—are they all sages?

sentences.zh: 顧學與不學耳。

translations.literal: It is only a matter of studying or not studying.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply a question of whether one studies or not.

sentences.zh: 朕修百官，興禮樂，其志固欲移風易俗。

translations.literal: I cultivate the hundred officials and raise rites and music; my aim firmly desires to shift customs and change habits.
translations.idiomatic: I have reformed the bureaucracy and revived ritual and music because I mean to transform the manners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕為天子，何必居中原！

translations.literal: I as Son of Heaven—why must I dwell in the Central Plain!
translations.idiomatic: Must an emperor live only in the Central Plains?

sentences.zh: 正欲卿等子孫漸染美俗，聞見廣博；

translations.literal: It is precisely wishing that your sons and grandsons gradually be steeped in fine customs and have broad hearing and seeing;
translations.idiomatic: I want your sons and grandsons to absorb refined customs and grow broad in knowledge and experience;

sentences.zh: 若永居恆北，復值不好文之主，不免面牆耳。」

translations.literal: If they forever dwell in the far north and again meet a lord who does not favor culture, they cannot escape facing-the-wall ignorance."
translations.idiomatic: but if they remain forever in the deep north under a ruler who scorns learning, they will end no better than men staring at a blank wall."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「誠如聖言。

translations.literal: He replied: "Truly it is as the sage words say.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rui answered: "Your Majesty speaks the truth.

sentences.zh: 金日磾不入仕漢朝，何能七世知名！」

translations.literal: Jin Midi, had he not entered service in the Han court, how could he have been famous for seven generations!"
translations.idiomatic: Had Jin Midi never entered Han service, how could his family have been renowned for seven generations!"

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王之廢也，鄱陽王鏘初不知謀。

translations.literal: When Prince Yulin was deposed, Prince of Poyang Xiao did not at first know the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, Prince Poyang Xiao had known nothing of the conspiracy at first.

sentences.zh: 及宣城公鸞權勢益重，中外皆知其蓄不臣之志。

translations.literal: When Duke of Xuancheng Luan's power and influence daily grew heavier, inside and outside all knew he harbored disloyal ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: As Duke Xuancheng Xiao Luan's power swelled, court and capital alike knew he nursed treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 鏘每詣鸞，鸞常屣履至車後迎之；

translations.literal: Each time Xiao visited Luan, Luan often in slippers went to behind the carriage to welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiao called on Luan, Luan would hurry out in slippers to meet his carriage;

sentences.zh: 語及家國，言淚俱發，鏘以此信之。

translations.literal: When speaking of family and state, words and tears together flowed; Xiao because of this trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: and when they spoke of the dynasty and the realm he wept as he spoke, so Xiao took him for a loyal kinsman.

sentences.zh: 宮台之內皆屬意於鏘，勸鏘入宮發兵輔政。

translations.literal: Within the palace terraces all placed their hopes on Xiao, urging Xiao to enter the palace and raise troops to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace everyone looked to Xiao and urged him to enter the palace, raise troops, and restore rightful rule.

sentences.zh: 制局監謝粲說鏘及隨王子隆曰：「二王但乘油壁車入宮，出天子置朝堂，夾輔號令；

translations.literal: Custodian of the Bureau Xie Can urged Xiao and Prince of Sui Zilong, saying: "The two princes need only ride oil-painted carriages into the palace, bring out the Son of Heaven and set him in the court hall, flank and assist the commands;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Can of the Bureau of Manufactories urged Xiao and Prince Sui Zilong: "Let the two of you ride your lacquered coaches into the palace, bring out the emperor and seat him in the hall, and rule jointly at his side;

sentences.zh: 粲等閉城門、上仗，誰敢不同！

translations.literal: Xie and the others will close the city gates and mount weapons—who dares not follow!
translations.idiomatic: we shall shut the gates and arm the guards—who would dare refuse!

sentences.zh: 東城人正共縛送蕭令耳。」

translations.literal: The people of the eastern city are just together binding and delivering Minister Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: The folk of the eastern quarter are even now ready to bind and deliver the Minister Xiao."

sentences.zh: 子隆欲定計。

translations.literal: Zilong wished to fix the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong was ready to commit to the plot.

sentences.zh: 鏘以上台兵力既悉度東府，且慮事不捷，意甚猶豫。

translations.literal: Xiao, because the superior terrace's military strength had already all been transferred to the Eastern Mansion and furthermore feared the affair would not succeed, was very hesitant in intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, however, knew that the palace guard had already been shifted to Luan's Eastern Mansion and feared failure, and he wavered badly.

sentences.zh: 馬隊主劉巨，世祖時舊人，詣鏘，請間，叩頭勸鏘立事。

translations.literal: Horse-corps chief Liu Ju, an old man from Emperor Shizu's time, went to Xiao, requested a private audience, kowtowed, and urged Xiao to undertake the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ju, chief of the horse guard and a veteran of the late Emperor Shizu's reign, sought a private audience with Xiao, kowtowed, and begged him to act.

sentences.zh: 鏘命駕將入，復還內，與母陸太妃別，日暮不成行。

translations.literal: Xiao ordered his carriage and was about to enter, but again returned inside to part from his mother Grand Consort Lu; the sun set without his completing the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao ordered out his carriage, then went back inside to bid farewell to his mother, Grand Consort Lu; dusk fell and he still had not set out.

sentences.zh: 典簽知其謀，告之。

translations.literal: The registry clerk knew their plot and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A registry clerk learned of the plot and informed Luan.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，鸞遣兵二千人圍鏘第，殺鏘，遂殺子隆及謝粲等。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Luan sent two thousand troops to surround Xiao's residence, killed Xiao, and then killed Zilong, Xie Can, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Luan sent two thousand men to surround Xiao's mansion, killed him, and then killed Zilong, Xie Can, and their confederates.

sentences.zh: 於時太祖諸子，子隆最壯大，有才能，故鸞尤忌之。

translations.literal: At that time among Emperor Taizu's sons, Zilong was the most robust and large and had ability and talent; therefore Luan especially feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the sons of the founding emperor, Zilong was the sturdiest and most capable, and Luan feared him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史晉安王子懋聞鄱陽、隨王死，欲起兵，謂防閣吳郡陸超之曰：「事成則宗廟獲安，不成猶為義鬼。」

translations.literal: Jin'an Prince Zimao, Governor of Jiang Province, hearing of the deaths of the Poyang and Sui princes, wished to raise troops and said to gate-guard Lu Chaozhi of Wu commandery: "If the affair succeeds, the ancestral temple obtains peace; if it does not succeed, I still become a righteous ghost."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin'an Zimao, governor of Jiang Province, learned that the princes of Poyang and Sui had been killed and resolved to raise an army. He told his gate-guard Lu Chaozhi of Wu: "If we succeed, the imperial house will be saved; if we fail, I shall die an honorable ghost."

sentences.zh: 防閣丹陽董僧慧曰：「此州雖小，宋孝武嘗用之。

translations.literal: Gate-guard Dong Senghui of Danyang said: "This province, though small, Emperor Xiaowu of Song once used it.
translations.idiomatic: His gate-guard Dong Senghui of Danyang said: "This province is small, yet Emperor Xiaowu of Song once made it the springboard for his throne.

sentences.zh: 若舉兵向闕以請鬱林之罪，誰能御之！」

translations.literal: If we raise troops toward the capital to request guilt for Yulin, who can resist!"
translations.idiomatic: March on the capital to demand justice for Yulin's deposition—who could withstand us!"

sentences.zh: 子懋母阮氏在建康，密遣書迎之，阮氏報其同母兄於瑤之為計。

translations.literal: Zimao's mother Lady Ruan was in Jiankang and secretly sent a letter welcoming him; Lady Ruan reported to her half-brother Yu Yaozhi to devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao's mother, Lady Ruan, was in Jiankang and secretly summoned him; she consulted her uterine brother Yu Yaozhi for advice.

sentences.zh: 瑤之馳告宣城公鸞；

translations.literal: Yaozhi galloped to inform Duke of Xuancheng Luan;
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi galloped to warn Duke Xuancheng Luan;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，假鸞黃鉞，內外纂嚴，遣中護軍王玄邈討子懋，又遣軍主裴叔業與於瑤之先襲尋陽，聲雲為郢府司馬。

translations.literal: On yihai, Luan was lent the yellow battle-axe; inside and outside were drawn to strict attention; he sent Central Guardian Wang Xuanyuan to attack Zimao, and also sent army commander Pei Shuye with Yu Yaozhi first to strike Xunyang, proclaiming to be the Ying prefecture's military aide.
translations.idiomatic: on yihai Luan was granted the imperial axe, martial law was proclaimed throughout the realm, and he dispatched the Central Guardian Wang Xuanyuan against Zimao while sending the commander Pei Shuye with Yu Yaozhi to strike Xunyang first, under the pretense that Pei was the Ying prefecture's deputy.

sentences.zh: 子懋知之，遣三百人守湓城。

translations.literal: Zimao knew of it and sent three hundred men to guard Pen city.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Zimao sent three hundred men to hold Pen Ford.

sentences.zh: 叔業溯流直上，至夜，回襲湓城；

translations.literal: Shuye went upstream direct; reaching night, he turned back to strike Pen city;
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sailed upstream, then under cover of night doubled back and stormed Pen Ford;

sentences.zh: 城局參軍樂賁開門納入。

translations.literal: Garrison bureau aide Yue Ben opened the gate and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ben, an aide in the city bureau, opened the gates and let them in.

sentences.zh: 子懋聞之，帥府州兵力據城自守。

translations.literal: Zimao, hearing of it, led the prefectural and provincial military strength to hold the city and defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zimao heard, he rallied the provincial army and barricaded himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 子懋部曲多雍州人，皆勇躍願奮。

translations.literal: Zimao's retainers were mostly men of Yong Province; all were brave, leaping, and wishing to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his personal troops were men of Yong Province, fierce and eager to fight.

sentences.zh: 叔業畏之，遣於瑤之說子懋曰：「今還都必無過憂，正當作散官，不失富貴也。」

translations.literal: Shuye feared them and sent Yu Yaozhi to persuade Zimao, saying: "If you now return to the capital, you will certainly have no excessive worry; you only ought to take a scattered official post and will not lose wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Shuye feared them and sent Yu Yaozhi to tell Zimao: "Return to the capital now and you will come to no harm—you will merely be given an honorific post and keep your wealth."

sentences.zh: 子懋既不出兵攻叔業，眾情稍沮。

translations.literal: Since Zimao did not send troops to attack Shuye, the crowd's mood gradually flagged.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao failed to strike at Shuye, and his men's spirit began to falter.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍於琳之，瑤之兄也，說子懋重賂叔業，可以免禍。

translations.literal: Central troops aide Yu Linzhi, Yaozhi's elder brother, urged Zimao to heavily bribe Shuye so he could avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Linzhi, a staff officer and Yaozhi's elder brother, advised Zimao that a heavy bribe to Shuye would spare him.

sentences.zh: 子懋使琳之往，琳之因說叔業取子懋。

translations.literal: Zimao sent Linzhi to go; Linzhi thereupon urged Shuye to seize Zimao.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao sent Linzhi to negotiate, but Linzhi instead urged Shuye to seize the prince.

sentences.zh: 叔業遣軍主徐玄慶將四百人隨琳之入州城，僚佐皆奔散。

translations.literal: Shuye sent army commander Xu Xuanqing leading four hundred men to follow Linzhi into the provincial city; the staff aides all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent Xu Xuanqing with four hundred men to follow Linzhi into the city; Zimao's officers fled in all directions.

sentences.zh: 琳之從二百人，拔白刃入齋，子懋罵曰：「小人！

translations.literal: Linzhi followed by two hundred men drew white blades and entered the study; Zimao cursed: "Petty man!
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi entered the prince's quarters with two hundred men, blades drawn. Zimao raged: "You wretch!

sentences.zh: 何忍行此！」

translations.literal: How can you bear to do this!"
translations.idiomatic: How could you bring yourself to this!"

sentences.zh: 琳之以袖障面，使人殺之。

translations.literal: Linzhi covered his face with his sleeve and had someone kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi hid his face in his sleeve and had his men cut Zimao down.

sentences.zh: 王玄邈執董僧慧，將殺之，僧慧曰：「晉安舉義兵，僕實預其謀；

translations.literal: Wang Xuanyuan seized Dong Senghui and was about to kill him; Senghui said: "Jin'an raised righteous troops; your servant truly participated in his plotting;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanyuan seized Dong Senghui to execute him. Senghui said: "Prince Jin'an raised a righteous army, and I took part in his counsel;

sentences.zh: 得為主人死，不恨矣！

translations.literal: to obtain death for my master—I have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: to die for one's lord is no regret!

sentences.zh: 願至大斂畢，退就鼎鑊。」

translations.literal: I wish to wait until the great encoffining is finished, then withdraw and submit to the cauldron."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me only that his funeral rites be completed, and then I will gladly go to the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 玄邈義之，具以白鸞；

translations.literal: Xuanyuan deemed him righteous and fully reported to Luan;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan was moved by his loyalty and reported the whole matter to Luan;

sentences.zh: 免死配東冶。

translations.literal: he was spared death and assigned to the Eastern smithy.
translations.idiomatic: who spared his life and sent him to labor in the eastern foundry.

sentences.zh: 子懋子昭基，九歲，以方二寸絹為書，參其消息，並遺錢五百，行金得達，僧慧視之曰：「郎君書也！」

translations.literal: Zimao's son Zhaoji, nine years old, used a square two-inch silk as a letter, checking his tidings, also sending five hundred cash; traveling gold enabled it to arrive; Senghui, viewing it, said: "The young master's writing!"
translations.idiomatic: Zimao's nine-year-old son Zhaoji wrote on a two-inch square of silk to ask after him and sent five hundred cash; couriers carried the message through. Senghui read it and cried, "It is the young lord's hand!"

sentences.zh: 悲慟而卒。

translations.literal: Grieved and anguished, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 於琳之勸陸超之逃亡，超之曰：「人皆有死，此不足懼！

translations.literal: Yu Linzhi urged Lu Chaozhi to flee; Chaozhi said: "All men have death—this is not enough to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Linzhi urged Lu Chaozhi to flee. Chaozhi said: "Every man must die—that is nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 吾若逃亡，非唯孤晉安之眷，亦恐田橫客笑人！」

translations.literal: If I flee, not only would I abandon Jin'an's kindness, I also fear Tian Heng's retainers would laugh at such men!"
translations.idiomatic: If I ran away I would betray Prince Jin'an's trust, and I should hate to make Tian Heng's loyal followers laugh at me!"

sentences.zh: 玄邈等欲囚以還都，超之端坐俟命。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan and the others wished to imprison him and return to the capital; Chaozhi sat upright awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan meant to take him captive to the capital; Chaozhi sat upright and waited for whatever might come.

sentences.zh: 超之門生謂殺超之當得賞，密自後斬之，頭墜而身不僵。

translations.literal: Chaozhi's student thought that killing Chaozhi ought to win a reward; secretly from behind he beheaded him—the head fell but the body did not stiffen.
translations.idiomatic: One of Chaozhi's students thought he would be rewarded for killing him and struck from behind; the head fell, yet the body remained upright.

sentences.zh: 玄邈厚加殯斂。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan lavishly added encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan gave him a lavish funeral.

sentences.zh: 門生亦助舉棺，棺墜，壓其首，折頸而死。

translations.literal: The student also helped lift the coffin; the coffin fell, crushed his head, and he broke his neck and died.
translations.idiomatic: The student helped bear the coffin; it slipped, crushed his head, and broke his neck—he died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 鸞遣平西將軍王廣之襲南兗州刺史安陸王子敬。

translations.literal: Luan sent Pacifier of the West Wang Guangzhi to strike Nan Yanzhou Governor Prince of Anlu Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Luan sent the Pacifier of the West Wang Guangzhi against Prince Anlu Zijing, governor of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣之至歐陽，遣部將濟陰陳伯之先驅。

translations.literal: Guangzhi reached Ouyang and sent subordinate general Chen Bozhi of Jiyin as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi reached Ouyang and sent his lieutenant Chen Bozhi of Jiyin ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 伯之因城開獨入，斬子敬。

translations.literal: Bozhi, taking advantage of the city gates opening, entered alone and beheaded Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: When the gates opened, Bozhi slipped in alone and slew Zijing.

sentences.zh: 鸞又遣徐玄慶西上害諸王。

translations.literal: Luan again sent Xu Xuanqing westward upriver to harm the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: Luan also sent Xu Xuanqing up the Yangzi to eliminate the remaining princes.

sentences.zh: 臨海王昭秀為荊州刺史，西中郎長史何昌寓行州事。

translations.literal: Prince of Linhai Zhaoxiu was Jingzhou Governor; Western Central Guard long-history He Changyu conducted provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linhai Zhaoxiu held Jing Province, with He Changyu of the Western Central Guard acting as regent of the province.

sentences.zh: 玄慶至江陵，欲以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Xuanqing reached Jiangling and wished to act according to convenience of circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanqing reached Jiangling he meant to kill the prince on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 昌寓曰：「僕受朝廷意寄，翼輔外籓。

translations.literal: Changyu said: "Your servant received the court's trust and charge, to flank and assist the outer fief.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu said: "I have been entrusted by the court to support this frontier fief.

sentences.zh: 殿下未有愆失，君以一介之使來，何容即以相付邪！

translations.literal: Your Highness has not yet fault or failure; you as a single envoy came—how allow immediately to hand him over!
translations.idiomatic: His Highness has done no wrong. You arrive as a lone envoy—how can you expect me simply to surrender him!

sentences.zh: 若朝廷必須殿下，當自啟聞，更聽後旨。」

translations.literal: If the court must have Your Highness, I should personally memorialize and report, and again listen for a later decree."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne truly requires the prince, I shall memorialize the capital and await further orders."

sentences.zh: 昭秀由是得還建康。

translations.literal: Zhaoxiu thereby was able to return to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this, Zhaoxiu was able to return alive to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 昌寓，尚之之弟子也。

translations.literal: Changyu was a nephew-disciple of He Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He Changyu was a nephew of the celebrated He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 鸞以吳興太宗孔琇之行郢州事，欲使之殺晉熙王銶。

translations.literal: Luan, because Kong Xiuzhi, Superintendent of Wuxing, was handling Yingzhou affairs, wished to have him kill the Prince of Jinxi, Xiao Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Luan meant to use Kong Xiuzhi, superintendent of Wuxing, who was already managing affairs at Yingzhou, to murder Prince Jinxi Xiao Qiao.

sentences.zh: 琇之辭不許，遂不食而死。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi declined and would not consent; thereupon he ceased eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi refused outright and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 琇之，靖之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was Jingzhi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was a grandson of Kong Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業自尋陽仍進向湘州，欲殺湘州刺史南平王銳，防閣周伯玉大言於眾曰：「此非天子意。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye from Xunyang still advanced toward Xiang Province, wishing to kill the Prince of Nanping, Xiao Rui, governor of Xiang Province; ward-officer Zhou Boyu spoke loudly before the crowd, saying: "This is not the Son of Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye marched on from Xunyang toward Xiangzhou, intending to kill the provincial governor, Prince Nanping Xiao Rui. The ward-officer Zhou Boyu cried out to the assembled troops: "This is not the emperor's order.

sentences.zh: 今斬叔業，舉兵匡社稷，誰敢不從！」

translations.literal: Now behead Shuye, raise troops to set right the altars of soil and grain—who dares not follow!"
translations.idiomatic: Slay Shuye now, take up arms to rescue the realm—who would refuse to follow!"

sentences.zh: 銳典簽叱左右斬之。

translations.literal: Rui's registry clerk shouted at those beside him to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's registry clerk ordered the guards to cut Boyu down at once.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，殺銳；

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Rui was killed;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Rui was put to death;

sentences.zh: 又殺郢州刺史晉熙王銶、南豫州刺史宜都王鏗。

translations.literal: again they killed the Prince of Jinxi, Xiao Qiao, governor of Ying Province, and the Prince of Yidu, Xiao Keng, governor of South Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: and with him fell Prince Jinxi Xiao Qiao, governor of Yingzhou, and Prince Yidu Xiao Keng, governor of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，廬陵王子卿為司徒，杜陽王鑠為中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, the Prince of Luling, Ziqing, became Minister of Education; the Prince of Duyang, Shuo, became General of the Central Army with Biaotong of the Three Excellencies and an open office.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince Luling Ziqing was made Minister of Education, and Prince Duyang Shuo was appointed General of the Central Army with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and authority to maintain a full staff.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，解嚴。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day dingyou, the emergency curfew was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingyou, the court ended the state of emergency.

sentences.zh: 以宣城公鸞為太傅、領大將軍、揚州牧、都督中外諸軍事，加殊禮，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Duke of Xuancheng Luan was made Grand Tutor, concurrently Grand General, governor of Yang Province, and commander of all military affairs within and without; extraordinary honors were added, and his rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuancheng Luan was made Grand Tutor, Grand General, and governor of Yangzhou, with overall command of armies at court and in the provinces; he received extraordinary ceremonial honors and was raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 宣城王謀繼大統，多引朝廷名士與參籌策。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuancheng plotted to succeed to the great succession and drew in many celebrated men of the court to take part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Xuancheng plotted to seize the throne, he enlisted many celebrated courtiers to help shape his strategy.

sentences.zh: 侍中謝朏心不願，乃求出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xie Tiao's heart was unwilling; he then requested to go out as governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xie Tiao wanted no part of it and asked to be sent away as governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 至郡，致酒數斛遺其弟吏部尚書瀹，為書曰：「可力飲此，勿豫人事！」

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery, he sent several hu of wine to his younger brother, Minister of the Civil Service Xie Yue, and wrote a letter saying: "You may drink this with all your strength—do not take part in human affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Once in his post he sent several hu of wine to his brother Yue, Minister of the Civil Service, with a note: "Drink this for all you are worth, and keep out of public affairs!"

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：臣聞「衣人之衣者懷人之憂，食人之食者死人之事。」

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Your subject has heard, "He who wears another's clothes bears another's worries; he who eats another's food dies for another's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: I have heard it said, "Whoever wears another man's coat must share his cares; whoever eats another man's bread must die in his service."

sentences.zh: 二謝兄弟，比肩貴近，安享榮祿，危不預知；

translations.literal: The two Xie brothers, shoulder to shoulder in noble proximity, peacefully enjoyed glory and stipend, yet did not foresee peril;
translations.idiomatic: The two Xie brothers stood shoulder to shoulder among the highest nobles, enjoying rank and salary in comfort, yet foresaw nothing of the coming danger;

sentences.zh: 為臣如此，可謂忠乎！

translations.literal: to be subjects like this—can it be called loyal!
translations.idiomatic: as ministers, can such conduct be called loyalty?

sentences.zh: 宣城王雖專國政，人情猶未服。

translations.literal: Although the Prince of Xuancheng monopolized state affairs, popular sentiment was still not submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Prince of Xuancheng already controlled the government, hearts had not yet submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 王胛上有赤志，驃騎咨議參軍考城江祐勸王出以示人。

translations.literal: On the prince's shoulder blade was a red birthmark; Rapid Cavalry staff adviser and military aide Jiang You of Kaocheng urged the prince to go out and show it to people.
translations.idiomatic: A red birthmark marked his shoulder blade. Jiang You of Kaocheng, a staff adviser on the Rapid Cavalry general's staff, urged him to display it in public.

sentences.zh: 王以示晉壽太守王洪範，曰：「人言此是日月相，卿幸勿洩！」

translations.literal: The prince showed it to Jinshou governor Wang Hongfan and said: "Men say this is a sun-and-moon physiognomy—please, by good fortune, do not leak it!"
translations.idiomatic: He showed it to Wang Hongfan, governor of Jinshou, and said: "People call this the mark of sun and moon together—you must not breathe a word of it!"

sentences.zh: 洪範曰：「公日月在軀，如何可隱，當轉言之！」

translations.literal: Hongfan said: "My lord, sun and moon are upon your person—how can it be hidden? It ought to be turned and spoken of!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan replied: "My lord carries sun and moon in your flesh—how could you hide it? You ought to let the story spread!"

sentences.zh: 王母，祏之姑也。

translations.literal: The prince's mother was Zhi's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's mother was an aunt of Jiang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 戊戈，殺桂陽王鑠、衡陽王鈞、江夏王鋒、建安王子真、巴陵王子倫。

translations.literal: On day wuge, the Princes of Guiyang, Shuo, Hengyang, Jun, Jiangxia, Feng, Jian'an, Zizhen, and Baling, Zilun, were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuge, Prince Guiyang Shuo, Prince Hengyang Jun, Prince Jiangxia Feng, Prince Jian'an Zizhen, and Prince Baling Zilun were executed.

sentences.zh: 鑠與鄱陽王鏘齊名；

translations.literal: Shuo and the Prince of Poyang, Xiao Qiang, were equal in fame;
translations.idiomatic: Shuo shared equal fame with Prince Poyang Xiao Qiang;

sentences.zh: 鏘好文章，鑠好名理，時人稱為鄱、桂。

translations.literal: Qiang loved literary compositions, Shuo loved name-principles; men of the time called them Po and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang delighted in letters, Shuo in philosophical disputation; contemporaries paired them as "Po and Gui."

sentences.zh: 鏘死，鑠不自安，至東府見宣城王，還，謂左右曰：「向錄公見接殷勤，流連不能已，而面有慚色，此必欲殺我。」

translations.literal: When Qiang died, Shuo was not at ease in himself; he went to the Eastern Headquarters to see the Prince of Xuancheng, returned, and said to those beside him: "Just now the Chief Recorder received me with earnest courtesy, lingering unable to stop, yet his face had a look of shame—this must mean he intends to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: After Qiang's death Shuo could not rest easy. He called at the Eastern Headquarters on the Prince of Xuancheng, and on returning told his attendants: "The Chief Recorder welcomed me with such pressing warmth that he could hardly let me go, yet shame showed in his face—he means to kill me."

sentences.zh: 是夕，遇害。

translations.literal: That same night, he met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he was slain.

sentences.zh: 宣城王每殺諸王，常夜遣兵圍其第，斬關逾垣，呼噪而入，家貲皆封籍之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Prince of Xuancheng killed the princes, he would commonly send troops by night to surround their mansions, cut the gate-bar and leap the walls, shouting and clamoring as they entered; household goods were all sealed and registered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Prince of Xuancheng killed a prince, he sent soldiers by night to surround the residence, break the gates, scale the walls, and burst in with a din; the household goods were then inventoried and sealed.

sentences.zh: 江夏王鋒，有才行，宣城王嘗與之言「遙光才力可委」。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, had ability and conduct; the Prince of Xuancheng once spoke with him of "Yaoguang's talent and strength being fit to entrust."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiangxia Feng was gifted and capable. The Prince of Xuancheng once remarked to him, "Yaoguang's talent and energy could be relied upon."

sentences.zh: 鋒曰：「遙光之於殿下，猶殿下之於高皇；

translations.literal: Feng said: "As for Yaoguang toward Your Highness, it is like Your Highness toward the High Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Feng said: "Yaoguang stands to Your Highness as Your Highness stood to the founding emperor;

sentences.zh: 衛宗廟，安社稷，實有攸寄。」

translations.literal: to guard the ancestral temple and settle the altars of soil and grain—truly there is that which may be entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: to guard the imperial temple and secure the realm—on him the dynasty may truly lean."

sentences.zh: 宣城王失色。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuancheng lost color.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuancheng turned pale.

sentences.zh: 及殺諸王，鋒遺宣城王書，誚責之；

translations.literal: When the princes were being killed, Feng left a letter to the Prince of Xuancheng, reviling and reproaching him;
translations.idiomatic: When the slaughter of the princes began, Feng sent the Prince of Xuancheng a letter of bitter reproach;

sentences.zh: 宣城王深憚之，不敢於第收鋒，使兼祠官於太廟，夜，遣兵廟中收之。

translations.literal: the Prince of Xuancheng deeply feared him, dared not seize Feng at his mansion, made him concurrently a temple officer at the Grand Ancestral Temple, and by night sent troops to seize him within the temple.
translations.idiomatic: deeply alarmed, the prince dared not take Feng at his mansion; he appointed him an auxiliary officer of sacrifice at the imperial temple, then sent soldiers by night to seize him there.

sentences.zh: 鋒出，登車，兵人欲上車，鋒有力，手擊數人皆仆地，然後死。

translations.literal: Feng came out, mounted the carriage; soldiers wished to mount the carriage—Feng had strength, and with his hands struck down several men, all falling to the ground; only then did he die.
translations.idiomatic: Feng came out and boarded the carriage. As the soldiers tried to climb in after him, he struck down several with his bare hands before they finally killed him.

sentences.zh: 宣城王遣典簽柯令孫殺建安王子真，子真走入床下，令孫手牽出之；

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuancheng sent registry clerk Ke Lingsun to kill the Prince of Jian'an, Zizhen; Zizhen ran under the bed, and Lingsun by hand dragged him out;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuancheng sent the registry clerk Ke Lingsun to kill Prince Jian'an Zizhen. Zizhen crawled under his bed; Lingsun hauled him out by hand;

sentences.zh: 叩頭乞為奴，不許而死。

translations.literal: he kowtowed begging to be made a slave; it was not permitted, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and begged to be kept alive as a slave. They refused, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 又遣中書舍人茹法亮殺巴陵王子倫。

translations.literal: He again sent Palace Secretariat attendant Ru Faliang to kill the Prince of Baling, Zilun.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Palace Secretariat attendant Ru Faliang to kill Prince Baling Zilun.

sentences.zh: 子倫性英果，時為南蘭陵太守，鎮琅邪，城有守兵。

translations.literal: Zilun's nature was heroic and resolute; at the time he was governor of South Lanling, garrisoning Langye, and the city had defending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun was bold and resolute. He then governed South Lanling from Langye, where the city still had a garrison.

sentences.zh: 宣城王恐不肯就死，以問典簽華伯茂。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuancheng feared he would not consent to die and questioned registry clerk Hua Bomao about it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zilun might resist, the Prince of Xuancheng consulted his registry clerk Hua Bomao.

sentences.zh: 伯茂曰：「公若以兵取之，恐不可即辦。

translations.literal: Bomao said: "If my lord takes him with troops, I fear it cannot be done at once.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao said: "If you mean to take him by force, that cannot be arranged quickly.

sentences.zh: 若委伯茂，一夫力耳。」

translations.literal: If you entrust it to Bomao, it is but the strength of one man."
translations.idiomatic: Entrust the matter to me, and one man's strength will suffice."

sentences.zh: 乃手自執鴆逼之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally took poison in hand and pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person with poisoned wine and forced Zilun to drink.

sentences.zh: 子倫正衣冠，出受詔，謂法亮曰：「先朝昔滅劉氏，今日之事，理數固然。

translations.literal: Zilun straightened cap and robes, came out to receive the edict, and said to Faliang: "The former court once extinguished the Liu house; today's affair is the pattern of principle and fate, as it must be.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun dressed properly, came out to receive the edict, and told Faliang: "Our dynasty once destroyed the house of Liu; what happens today follows the same inexorable pattern.

sentences.zh: 君是身家舊人，今銜此使，當由事不獲已。

translations.literal: You are an old man of our household; now bearing this commission, it must be because the affair could not be helped.
translations.idiomatic: You are a man of our household from of old; in carrying out this charge you act only because you cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 此酒非勸酬之爵。」

translations.literal: This wine is not a cup for urging mutual toasts."
translations.idiomatic: This cup is not offered for polite drinking."

sentences.zh: 因仰之而死，時年十六。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised it and died; he was sixteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the cup, drank, and died. He was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 法亮及左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: Faliang and those beside him all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang and his attendants wept.

sentences.zh: 初，諸王出鎮，皆置典簽，主帥一方之事，悉以委之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when the princes went out to garrison posts, each was given a registry clerk; affairs commanding a region were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, whenever a prince took up a provincial command, a registry clerk was appointed, and nearly all local authority was placed in his hands.

sentences.zh: 時入奏事，一歲數返，時主輒與之間語，訪以州事，刺史美惡專系其口。

translations.literal: They would enter to report affairs several times in a year; the ruler would then converse privately with them, inquiring about provincial affairs, and whether a governor was good or bad depended solely on their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to court several times a year to report; the emperor would speak with them privately and ask after provincial affairs, so that a governor's reputation depended entirely on what they said.

sentences.zh: 自刺史以下莫不折節奉之，恆慮弗及。

translations.literal: From governors downward, none failed to bend their conduct in serving them, always fearing they would not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: From the governor down, everyone humbled himself before them, always afraid of falling short.

sentences.zh: 於是威行州部，大為奸利。

translations.literal: Thereupon their authority ran through the provinces and departments, and they greatly wrought villainous profit.
translations.idiomatic: Their power spread through every province, and they grew rich on corruption.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄為江州，性烈直，不可干；

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling, Ye, was in Jiang Province; his nature was fierce and upright, and could not be approached;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuling Ye held Jiangzhou. He was fierce and upright, and could not be tampered with;

sentences.zh: 典簽趙渥之謂人曰：「今出都易刺史！」

translations.literal: registry clerk Zhao Wozhi said to others: "Now leaving the capital makes a governor easy to replace!"
translations.idiomatic: yet his registry clerk Zhao Wozhi told acquaintances: "Once I reach the capital, changing a governor will be easy!"

sentences.zh: 及見世祖，盛毀之；

translations.literal: When he saw Emperor Shizu, he lavishly slandered him;
translations.idiomatic: At court he slandered Ye before Emperor Shizu without restraint;

sentences.zh: 曄遂免還。

translations.literal: Ye was thereupon dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: and Ye was recalled and stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 南海王子罕戍琅邪，欲暫游東堂，典簽姜秀不許。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanhai, Zihan, garrisoned Langye and wished to stroll for a time to the Eastern Hall; registry clerk Jiang Xiu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Nanhai Zihan, posted at Langye, wished to stroll to the Eastern Hall for a time, but registry clerk Jiang Xiu refused permission.

sentences.zh: 子罕還，泣謂母曰：「兒欲移五步亦不得，與囚何異！」

translations.literal: Zihan returned, weeping, and said to his mother: "Your son wishes to move five paces yet cannot—how does he differ from a prisoner!"
translations.idiomatic: Zihan went back inside weeping and told his mother: "I cannot walk five steps on my own—what am I but a prisoner!"

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子貞嘗求熊白，廚人答典簽不在，不敢與。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shaoling, Zizhen, once asked for bear's palm; the cook answered that the registry clerk was not present and dared not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoling Zizhen once asked for bear's palm; the cook replied that the registry clerk was away and he dared not serve it.

sentences.zh: 永明中，巴東王子響殺劉寅等，世祖聞之，謂群臣曰：「子響遂反！」

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, the Prince of Badong, Zixiang, killed Liu Yin and others; Emperor Shizu, hearing of it, said to the assembled ministers: "Zixiang has finally rebelled!"
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming reign, Prince Badong Zixiang killed Liu Yin and his party. When Emperor Shizu heard of it he told the ministers: "Zixiang has rebelled at last!"

sentences.zh: 戴僧靜大言曰：「諸王都自應反，豈唯巴東！」

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing spoke loudly: "All the princes ought by themselves to rebel—how is it only Badong!"
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing cried out: "Every prince ought to rebel—why speak only of Badong!"

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「天生無罪，而一時被囚，取一挺藕，一杯漿，皆咨簽帥；

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Born without crime, yet for a time imprisoned—to take one stalk of lotus root, one cup of gruel, all must be referred to the registry commander;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. He answered: "They are born innocent, yet live as captives. To take a lotus root or a cup of gruel they must ask the registry commander;

sentences.zh: 簽帥不在，則竟日忍渴。

translations.literal: when the registry commander is not present, they endure thirst the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: and if he is absent they go thirsty all day.

sentences.zh: 諸州唯聞有簽帥，不聞有刺史。

translations.literal: In all the provinces one hears only of registry commanders, not of governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces one hears only of registry commanders, never of governors.

sentences.zh: 何得不反！」

translations.literal: How can they not rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: How could they not rebel!"

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良嘗問眾曰：「士大夫何意詣簽帥？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, once asked the assembly: "What is the gentry's intent in calling on registry commanders?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling Ziliang once asked his staff: "Why do gentlemen of rank go to pay court to registry commanders?"

sentences.zh: 參軍范雲曰：「詣長史以下皆無益，詣簽帥立有倍本之價。

translations.literal: Military aide Fan Yun said: "Calling on anyone below the chief administrator is without profit; calling on a registry commander at once has double-the-capital value.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Fan Yun replied: "Visits to anyone below the chief administrator bring no return; a visit to a registry commander doubles your capital at once.

sentences.zh: 不詣謂何！」

translations.literal: If one does not call on them, what would you say!"
translations.idiomatic: Why should they not go!"

sentences.zh: 子良有愧色。

translations.literal: Ziliang had a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 及宣城王誅諸王，皆令典簽殺之，竟無一人能抗拒者。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xuancheng executed the princes, he ordered registry clerks to kill them; in the end not one man could resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xuancheng slaughtered the princes, he had their registry clerks do the killing, and not one prince could resist.

sentences.zh: 孔珪聞之，流涕曰：「齊之衡陽、江夏最有意，而復害之；

translations.literal: Kong Gui, hearing of it, shed tears and said: "Among Qi, Hengyang and Jiangxia had the most purpose, yet again they were harmed;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui wept when he heard it and said: "Of all the princes of Qi, Hengyang and Jiangxia had the finest spirit, yet they too were destroyed;

sentences.zh: 若不立簽帥，故當不至於此。」

translations.literal: if registry commanders had not been established, by rights it ought not to have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: had registry commanders never been created, things would never have reached this pass."

sentences.zh: 宣城王亦深知典簽之弊，乃詔：「自今諸州有急事，當密以奏聞，勿復遣典簽入都。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuancheng also deeply knew the registry clerks' abuse, and thereupon decreed: "From now on, when the provinces have urgent affairs, they should be secretly reported to the court; do not again send registry clerks into the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuancheng, well aware of the evil the registry clerks had wrought, issued an edict: "Henceforth urgent provincial matters shall be reported to the throne in secret; registry clerks must no longer be sent to the capital."

sentences.zh: 自是典簽之任浸輕矣。

translations.literal: From this time the registry clerks' duties gradually grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the power of the registry clerks steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 蕭子顯論曰：帝王之子，生長富厚，期出閨閫，暮司方岳，防驕翦逸，積代常典。

translations.literal: Xiao Zixian's discourse says: Sons of emperors and kings, growing up in wealth and plenty, at dawn leave the inner quarters, at dusk administer regional mountains—guarding against arrogance and cutting off excess is the constant canon of successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zixian comments: Imperial sons are reared in wealth; at dawn they leave the palace, by evening they govern a province. To curb pride and restrain license has been the rule of every age.

sentences.zh: 故輔以上佐，簡自帝心；

translations.literal: Therefore they are assisted with senior aides, chosen from the emperor's own heart;
translations.idiomatic: So they are given senior aides chosen by the throne itself;

sentences.zh: 勞舊左右，用為主帥，飲食游居，動應聞啟；

translations.literal: veterans of long service at the ruler's side are used as commanders-in-chief; eating, drinking, roaming, and dwelling—all movements must be heard and reported.
translations.idiomatic: trusted veterans of the palace are made their chiefs of staff; every meal, outing, or move of the day must be reported.

sentences.zh: 處地雖重，行己莫由。

translations.literal: Though their position in the land is weighty, in conducting themselves they have no way of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Their posts may be weighty, yet they cannot act on their own.

sentences.zh: 威不在身，恩未下及，一朝艱難總至，望其釋位扶危，何可得矣！

translations.literal: Authority is not upon their persons, favor has not reached down to them—when in one morning hardship altogether arrives, to hope they will yield position and support peril, how can it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: They wield no real power and win no real loyalty; when crisis strikes at once, to expect them to step aside and save the state—how could that be possible?

sentences.zh: 斯宋氏之餘風，至齊室而尤弊也。

translations.literal: This is the remnant wind of the Song house; reaching the Qi court it became especially corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the lingering habit of the Song dynasty, and under Qi it grew worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以寧朔將軍蕭遙欣為豫州刺史，黃門郎蕭遙昌為郢州刺史，輔國將軍蕭誕為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On day guimao, General Who Pacifies the North Xiao Yaoxin was made governor of Yu Province; Yellow Gate Gentleman Xiao Yaochang was made governor of Ying Province; General Who Assists the State Xiao Dan was made governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, General Who Pacifies the North Xiao Yaoxin was appointed governor of Yuzhou; Yellow Gate Gentleman Xiao Yaochang governor of Yingzhou; and General Who Assists the State Xiao Dan governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 遙昌，遙欣之弟；

translations.literal: Yaochang was Yaoxin's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Yaochang was the younger brother of Yaoxin;

sentences.zh: 誕，諶之兄也。

translations.literal: Dan was Zhen's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was the elder brother of Xiao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏以太尉東陽王丕為太傅、錄尚書事，留守平城。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Wei made Grand Commandant the Prince of Dongyang, Pi, Grand Tutor and recorder of affairs for the Masters of Writing, remaining to guard Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Northern Wei appointed Grand Commandant Prince Dongyang Pi Grand Tutor and recorder of affairs for the Masters of Writing, with orders to remain and guard Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主親告太廟，使高陽王雍、於列奉遷神主於洛陽；

translations.literal: On day wushen, the Wei ruler personally announced at the Grand Temple, sending the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, and Yu Lie to escort and move the spirit tablets to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Wei emperor announced the move at the Grand Ancestral Temple in person and sent Prince Gaoyang Yong and Yu Lie to convey the spirit tablets to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 辛亥，發平城。

translations.literal: on day xinhai, he set out from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on xinhai he departed from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 海陵王在位，起居飲食，皆咨宣城王而後行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hailing, on the throne, in rising, resting, eating, and drinking—all consulted the Prince of Xuancheng before acting.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Hailing sat on the throne, every act of daily life—rising, resting, eating, drinking—required the Prince of Xuancheng's approval.

sentences.zh: 嘗思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。

translations.literal: He once wished to eat steamed fish and vegetables; the Grand Provisioner replied that without the Chief Recorder's order, in the end it was not given.
translations.idiomatic: Once he craved steamed fish and greens; the palace provisioner answered that without the Chief Recorder's command nothing could be served, and he went without.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令曰：「嗣主沖幼，庶政多昧；

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the Empress Dowager's order said: "The successor ruler is young and tender, and the many affairs of government are obscure;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Empress Dowager issued an edict: "The heir to the throne is young, and public affairs are beyond him;

sentences.zh: 且早嬰尪疾，弗克負荷。

translations.literal: moreover, from early youth he has been afflicted with wasting illness and cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: moreover he has been frail from childhood and cannot bear the burden of rule.

sentences.zh: 太傅宣城王，胤體宣皇，鐘慈太祖，宜入承寶命。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, by blood-line the body of the Proclaimed Emperor, concentrating kindness from the Grand Ancestor, ought to enter and receive the precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, born of the imperial line and cherished by the founding emperor, should ascend and receive the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 帝可降封海陵王，吾當歸老別館。」

translations.literal: The emperor may be demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing; I shall return to age in a separate lodge."
translations.idiomatic: Let the emperor be demoted to Prince Hailing; I shall retire to a separate palace."

sentences.zh: 且以宣城王為太祖第三子。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Xuancheng was treated as the Grand Ancestor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: The court also declared the Prince of Xuancheng to be the founding emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，高宗即皇帝位，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On day guihai, the High Ancestor assumed the imperial position, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Emperor Ming took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 以太尉王敬則為大司馬，司空陳顯達為太尉，尚書令王晏加驃騎大將軍，左僕射徐孝嗣加中軍大將軍，中領軍蕭諶為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal; Minister of Works Chen Xianda was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was added as Rapid Cavalry Grand General; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was added as General of the Central Army; Central Palace Guard Commander Xiao Zhen was made Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal, Chen Xianda Grand Commandant, Wang Yan Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Xu Xiaosi General of the Central Army, and Xiao Zhen Commander of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 度支尚書虞悰稱疾不陪位。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Yu Song claimed illness and did not attend the enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song, Minister of Revenue, pleaded illness and did not attend the enthronement.

sentences.zh: 帝以悰舊人，欲引參佐命，使王晏繼廢立事示悰。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Song was an old acquaintance, wished to draw him in to assist the mandate; he had Wang Yan continue the account of deposition and enthronement to show Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Song as an old associate, wished to enlist him in the new order and had Wang Yan recount the deposition and enthronement for his benefit.

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以贊惟新乎！

translations.literal: Song said: "The ruler above is sagely and bright, the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—how could one borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal!
translations.idiomatic: Song said: "Your Majesty is sage and brilliant, and the ministers serve with one accord—why borrow a worn-out old man for the renewal of the state!

sentences.zh: 不敢聞命！」

translations.literal: dare not hear command!"
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept such a command!"

sentences.zh: 因慟哭。

translations.literal: thereupon wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: And thereupon he broke into bitter weeping.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲糾之，徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」

translations.literal: court deliberation wished to impeach him, Xu Xiaosi said: "this also is antiquity's surviving straightness."
translations.idiomatic: The court debated punishing him; Xu Xiaosi said, "This, too, is a remnant of the ancient type who spoke straight to power."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And they desisted.

sentences.zh: 帝與群臣宴會，詔功臣上酒。

translations.literal: emperor with ministers banquet, ordered meritorious ministers offer wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted with his ministers and ordered meritorious officials to offer toasts.

sentences.zh: 王晏等興席，謝瀹獨不起，曰：「陛下受命，應天順人；

translations.literal: Wang Yan and others rose from seats, Xie Yue alone did not rise, said: "Your Majesty received Mandate, responded to Heaven followed people;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and the others rose from their seats; Xie Yue alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the Mandate, harmonizing with Heaven and following the people;

sentences.zh: 王晏妄叨天功以為己力！」

translations.literal: Wang Yan presumptuously usurps Heaven's merit as his own strength!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement!"

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，解之。

translations.literal: emperor great laugh, excused him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 座罷，晏呼瀹共載還令省，欲相撫悅。

translations.literal: seats ended, Yan called Yue share carriage return to Ministry office, wished mutually to soothe and please.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended, Yan summoned Yue to ride back with him to the Ministry of Justice, hoping to win him over.

sentences.zh: 瀹正色曰：「君巢窟在何處！」

translations.literal: Yue stern countenance said: "my lord's nest den at what place!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said with a stern face, "Where is your nest and den!"

sentences.zh: 晏甚憚之。

translations.literal: Yan greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply intimidated by him.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔：「籓牧守宰，或有薦獻，事非任土，悉加禁斷。」

translations.literal: dingmao, edict: "feudal lords governors prefects magistrates, some have presented tribute, matters not local products, all add prohibition cut off."
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, an edict proclaimed: "Where governors, prefects, and magistrates present offerings that are not the fixed products of their jurisdictions, all such gifts are strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏主如信都。

translations.literal: jisi, Wei sovereign went to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, the Wei sovereign went to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 庚午，曰：「比聞緣邊之蠻，多竊掠南土，使父子乖離，室家分絕。

translations.literal: gengwu, said: "of late heard border barbarians, many stealthily plundered southern lands, made fathers sons estranged, households families separated cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, he said, "Of late I have heard that frontier tribes along the borders often steal southward, tearing fathers from sons and breaking households apart.

sentences.zh: 聯方蕩壹區宇，子育萬姓，若苟如此，南人豈知朝德哉！

translations.literal: Lian about to sweep unify one realm, nurture myriad people, if thus carelessly, southern people how know court virtue!
translations.idiomatic: We are about to pacify and unify the realm and nurture the myriad people—if things go on thus, how will southerners know the court's virtue!

sentences.zh: 可詔荊、郢、東荊三州，禁勒蠻民，勿有侵暴。」

translations.literal: may order Jing, Ying, East Jing three provinces, restrain barbarian peoples, do not have invasion violence."
translations.idiomatic: Order the three provinces of Jing, Ying, and East Jing to restrain the barbarian peoples and forbid all aggression."

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸酉，以始安王遙光為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: eleventh month, guiyou, made Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang Yang Province governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the guiyou day, Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang was appointed governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，魏主如鄴。

translations.literal: dingchou, Wei sovereign went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day, the Wei sovereign went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，立皇子寶義為晉安王，寶玄為江夏王，寶源為廬陵王，寶寅為建安王，寶融為隨郡王，寶攸為南平王。

translations.literal: gengchen, installed imperial sons Bao Yi as Prince of Jin'an, Bao Xuan as Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Yuan as Prince of Luling, Bao Yin as Prince of Jian'an, Bao Rong as Prince of Sui Commandery, Bao You as Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, the princes were enfeoffed: Bao Yi as Prince of Jin'an, Bao Xuan as Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Yuan as Prince of Luling, Bao Yin as Prince of Jian'an, Bao Rong as Prince of Sui Commandery, and Bao You as Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔曰：「邑宰祿薄，雖任土恆貢，自今悉斷。」

translations.literal: jiashen, edict said: "district magistrates' salaries thin, though local products constant tribute, from now all cut off."
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, an edict declared: "District magistrates' salaries are meager; though fixed local tribute has long been the custom, from this day forward all such offerings are abolished."

sentences.zh: 乙酉，追尊始安貞王為景皇，妃為懿後。

translations.literal: yiyou, posthumously honored late Prince of Shi'an Zhen as Jing Emperor, consort as Empress Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day, the late Prince of Shi'an Zhen was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, and his consort as Empress Yi.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以聞喜公遙欣為荊州刺史，豐城公遙昌為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: bingxu, made Duke of Wenxi Yao Xin Jing Province governor, Duke of Fengcheng Yao Chang Yu Province governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day, Duke of Wenxi Yao Xin was made governor of Jing Province and Duke of Fengcheng Yao Chang governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 時上長子晉安王寶義有廢疾，諸子皆弱小，故以遙光居中，遙欣鎮撫上流。

translations.literal: at this time sovereign's eldest son Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi had crippling illness, all sons all young weak, therefore used Yao Guang at center, Yao Xin guard pacify upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor's eldest son, Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi, was disabled by illness and all the other sons were still young; therefore Yao Guang was placed at the center while Yao Xin guarded and pacified the upper Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立皇子寶卷為太子。

translations.literal: wuzi, installed imperial son Bao Juan as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day, Prince Bao Juan was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 魏主至洛陽，欲澄清流品，以尚書崔亮兼吏部郎。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign reached Luoyang, wished to clarify flowing ranks, made Minister Cui Liang concurrently Personnel Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign reached Luoyang and wished to clarify pedigree ranks, appointing Minister Cui Liang concurrently as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 亮，道固之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Liang, Daogu's elder brother's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was the grandson of Daogu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 魏主敕後軍將軍寧文福行牧地。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign ordered Rear Army General Ning Wenfu survey pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign ordered Rear Army General Ning Wenfu to survey pasturage lands.

sentences.zh: 福表石濟以西，河內以東，距河凡十里。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized Shiji west, Henei east, from river altogether ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu memorialized: west of Shiji, east of Henei, ten li from the river throughout.

sentences.zh: 魏主自代徙雜畜置其地，使福掌之；

translations.literal: Wei sovereign from Dai moved miscellaneous livestock placed on this land, made Fu manage it;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign moved miscellaneous herds from Dai and placed them on this land, putting Wenfu in charge;

sentences.zh: 畜無耗失，以為司馬監。

translations.literal: livestock without waste loss, made him Grand Equerry-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: not a beast was lost to waste, and he was appointed Grand Equerry-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖平統萬及秦、涼，以河西水草豐美，用為牧地，畜甚蕃息，馬至二百餘萬匹，橐駝半之，牛羊無數。

translations.literal: at first, Shizu pacified Tongwan and Qin, Liang, because Hexi grass water abundant beautiful, used as pasture land, livestock very multiplied, horses reached two hundred-odd ten thousand head, camels half that, cattle sheep countless.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Emperor Shizu pacified Tongwan, Qin, and Liang, the lush grass and water of the Hexi region made excellent pasture; herds multiplied greatly—horses reached more than two million head, camels half that number, cattle and sheep beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 及高祖置牧場於河陽，常畜戌馬十萬匹，每歲自河西徙牧并州，稍復南徙，欲其漸習水土，不至死傷，而河西之牧愈更蕃滋。

translations.literal: when Gaozu placed pasture at Heyang, constantly kept garrison horses hundred thousand head, each year from Hexi moved pasture to Bing Province, gradually again south moved, wished them gradually accustom soil water, not reach death injury, while Hexi pastures ever more multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu established pastures at Heyang, he regularly kept one hundred thousand war horses; each year herds were driven from Hexi to graze at Bing Province, then gradually moved farther south, wishing them to accustom themselves to soil and water so they would not die or suffer injury, while Hexi pastures grew ever more abundant.

sentences.zh: 及正光以後，皆為寇盜所掠，無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: when Zhengguang afterward, all by raiders bandits plundered, none left surviving.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengguang era, all were plundered by raiders and bandits, not one left alive.

sentences.zh: 永明中，御史中丞沈淵表，百官年七十，皆令致仕，並窮困私門。

translations.literal: in Yongming, Vice Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan memorialized, all officials age seventy, all ordered retire, all impoverished confined private gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era, Vice Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan memorialized that all officials aged seventy should be made to retire and confined to penury in their private households.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔依舊銓敘。

translations.literal: gengzi, edict according to former evaluation and ranking.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, an edict ordered evaluation according to the former practice.

sentences.zh: 上輔政所誅諸王，皆復屬籍，封其子為侯。

translations.literal: sovereign regency executed princes, all restored clan registers, enfeoffed their sons as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The princes executed during the regency were all restored to the imperial clan rolls, and their sons were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 上詐稱海陵恭王有疾，數遣御師瞻視，因而殞之，葬禮並依漢東海恭王故事。

translations.literal: sovereign falsely claimed Prince of Hailing Gong had illness, repeatedly sent imperial physicians observe, thereby caused his death, funeral rites all according to Han Prince of Donghai Gong precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor falsely claimed that Prince of Hailing Gong was ill, repeatedly sent imperial physicians to examine him, and thereby caused his death; the funeral followed the precedent of the Han Prince of Donghai Gong.

sentences.zh: 魏郢州刺史韋珍，在州有聲績，魏主賜以駿馬、谷帛。

translations.literal: Wei Ying Province Governor Wei Zhen, in province had renowned record, Wei sovereign bestowed fine horses, grain silks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen, governor of Ying Province, had a renowned record in office; the Wei sovereign bestowed fine horses and grain and silks.

sentences.zh: 珍集境內孤貧者，悉散與之，謂之曰：「天子以我能綏撫卿等，故賜以谷帛，吾何敢獨有之！」

translations.literal: Zhen gathered within borders orphaned poor, all distributed to them, said to them: "Son of Heaven because I can comfort settle you all, therefore bestowed grain silks, how dare I alone possess it!"
