translations.idiomatic: Zhen gathered the orphaned and poor within his jurisdiction and distributed everything among them, saying, "The Son of Heaven rewarded me because I can comfort and settle you—how dare I keep it all for myself!"

sentences.zh: 魏主以上廢海陵王自立，謀大舉入寇。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign because above deposed Prince of Hailing self-established, planned great campaign invade.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qi had deposed the Prince of Hailing and the Wei sovereign had himself seized the throne, he planned a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 會邊將言，雍州刺史下邳曹虎遣使請降於魏，十一月，辛丑朔，魏遣行征南將軍薛真度督四將向襄陽，大將軍劉昶、平南將軍王肅向義陽，徐州刺史拓跋衍向鐘離，平南將軍廣平劉藻向南鄭。

translations.literal: met border generals report, Yong Province Governor Xiapi Cao Hu sent envoys request surrender to Wei, eleventh month xinchou new moon, Wei dispatched Acting General Who Conquers South Xue Zhendu supervised four generals toward Xiangyang, Grand General Liu Chang, General Who Pacifies South Wang Su toward Yiyang, Xu Province Governor Tuoba Yan toward Zhongli, General Who Pacifies South Guangping Liu Zao toward Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that border commanders reported that Cao Hu, governor of Yong and native of Xiapi, had sent envoys offering surrender to Wei; on the new moon of xinchou in the eleventh month, Wei dispatched Acting General Who Conquers the South Xue Zhendu supervising four generals toward Xiangyang, Grand General Liu Chang and General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su toward Yiyang, Governor of Xu Province Tuoba Yan toward Zhongli, and General Who Pacifies the South Liu Zao of Guangping toward Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 真度，安都從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Zhendu, Andu's father's-line younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu was a younger cousin of Andu on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 以尚書盧淵為安南將軍，督襄陽前鋒諸軍。

translations.literal: made Minister Lu Yuan General Who Pacifies South, supervised Xiangyang vanguard all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Yuan was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, commanding the vanguard forces at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 淵辭以不習軍旅，不許。

translations.literal: Yuan declined on grounds not versed in military affairs, not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with military affairs; this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「但恐曹虎為周魴耳。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "only fear Cao Hu is Zhou Fang."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "I only fear Cao Hu will prove another Zhou Fang."

sentences.zh: 魏主欲變易舊風，壬寅，詔禁士民胡服。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign wished transform old customs, renyin, edict forbade scholars commoners Hu dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign wished to transform the old customs; on the renyin day, an edict forbade commoners and officials Hu-style dress.

sentences.zh: 國人多不悅。

translations.literal: state's people many not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Many throughout the state were displeased.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍劉芳，纘之族弟也，與給事黃門侍郎太原郭祚，皆以文學為帝所親禮，多引與講論及密議政事；

translations.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Fang, Zuan's clansman younger brother, with Supervisor of Secretariat Taiyuan Guo Zuo, all by literary learning by emperor intimately honored, often drawn into discussions and secret deliberations state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Fang, a clansman of Liu Zuan, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Guo Zuo of Taiyuan were both treated with intimate favor by the emperor for their literary learning; he often drew them into discussions and private deliberations on state affairs;

sentences.zh: 大臣貴戚皆以為疏己，怏怏有不平之色。

translations.literal: great ministers noble kin all considered estranged themselves, resentful had discontented expressions.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers and noble kin all felt themselves estranged and showed discontent on their faces.

sentences.zh: 帝使給事黃門侍郎陸覬私諭之曰：「至尊但欲廣知古事，詢訪前世法式耳，終不親彼而相疏也。」

translations.literal: emperor made Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them said: "Sovereign only wishes broaden knowledge ancient matters, inquire former ages institutions, that is all, ultimately will not favor them and estrange you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them, saying, "His Majesty only wishes to broaden his knowledge of antiquity and inquire into institutions of former ages—that is all; he will never favor them and distance you."

sentences.zh: 眾意乃稍解。

translations.literal: crowd's resentment then slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd's resentment gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 覬，□之子也。

translations.literal: Guan, □'s son.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was the son of [name lost in the source].

sentences.zh: 魏主欲自將入寇。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign wished personally lead invasion.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign wished to lead the invasion in person.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: guimao, within and without martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, court and countryside were placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔代民遷洛者復租賦三年。

translations.literal: wushen, edict Dai people moved to Luoyang restored rent taxes three years.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, an edict exempted those who had moved from Dai to Luoyang from rent and tax for three years.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史高閭上表稱：「洛陽草創，曹虎既不遣質任，必非誠心，無宜輕舉。」

translations.literal: Xiang Province Governor Gao Lu memorialized: "Luoyang newly founded, Cao Hu since did not send hostages, certainly not sincere heart, no grounds rash move."
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Xiang Province Gao Lu memorialized: "Luoyang is newly founded; since Cao Hu has sent no hostages, his sincerity is doubtful—there is no grounds for a rash move."

sentences.zh: 魏主不從。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign did not heed this.

sentences.zh: 久之，虎使竟不再來，魏主引公卿議行留之計，公卿或以為宜止，或以為宜行。

translations.literal: after long while, Hu's envoys ultimately never came again, Wei sovereign summoned nobles ministers discuss go stay plans, nobles ministers some held should halt, some held should go.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, Cao Hu's envoys never came again; the Wei sovereign summoned the nobles and ministers to discuss whether to march or stay—some held they should halt, some that they should go.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「眾人紛紜，莫知所從。

translations.literal: emperor said: "crowd clamorous, none knows what to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everyone clamors and none knows what to follow.

sentences.zh: 必欲盡行留之勢，宜有客主，共相起發。

translations.literal: must wish exhaust go stay's cases, should have guest host, mutually prompt each other.
translations.idiomatic: If we are to exhaust the case for going and staying, there should be guest and host, each prompting the other.

sentences.zh: 任城、鎮南為留議，朕為行論，諸公坐聽得矣，長者從之。」

translations.literal: Rencheng, Guards South for stay argument, We for go argument, you gentlemen sit listen suffices, elder follow it."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng and the General Who Guards the South will argue for staying; I will argue for marching—you gentlemen sit and listen, and that will suffice; you may follow the elder's view."

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: all said: "yes."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍李沖曰：「臣等正以遷都草創，人思少安；

translations.literal: General Who Guards South Li Chong said: "we ministers just because capital moved newly founded, people wish little peace;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the South Li Chong said, "We ministers hold that the capital has just been moved and the people yearn for a little peace;

sentences.zh: 為內應者未得審諦，不宜輕動。」

translations.literal: those who would respond from within not yet obtained careful verification, not suitable rash move."
translations.idiomatic: those who would respond from within have not yet been verified in detail—it is inadvisable to move rashly."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼降款虛實，誠未可知。

translations.literal: emperor said: "their surrender false true, indeed not yet knowable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whether their surrender is false or true is indeed unknown.

sentences.zh: 若其虛也，朕巡撫淮甸，訪民疾苦，使彼知君德之所在，有北向之心；

translations.literal: if it is false, We tour console Huai region, inquire people's hardships, make them know sovereign virtue's place, have northward-turning hearts;
translations.idiomatic: If it is false, I shall tour and console the Huai region, inquire into the people's hardships, and let them know where sovereign virtue resides, so they acquire a mind to turn northward;

sentences.zh: 若其實也，今不以時應接，則失乘時之機，孤歸義之誠，敗朕大略矣。」

translations.literal: if it is true, now not by season respond connect, then lose seize season's opportunity, betray come-over's sincerity, ruin Our grand design."
translations.idiomatic: if it is true, not to respond in season now means losing the opportune moment, betraying the sincerity of those who came over, and ruining my grand design."

sentences.zh: 任城王洽曰：「虎無質任，又使不再來，其詐可知也。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng He said: "Hu had no hostages, again envoys never came, his deception can be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng He said, "Hu sent no hostages, and his envoys never came again—his deception is plain.

sentences.zh: 今代都新遷之民，皆有戀本之心。

translations.literal: now Dai capital newly moved people, all have cling-to-home hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people newly moved from Dai all have hearts that cling to their old home.

sentences.zh: 扶老攜幼，始就洛邑，居無一椽之室，食無甔石之儲。

translations.literal: supporting old leading young, just reached Luoyang city, dwell without one rafter's room, eat without dou-stone's stores.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting the old and leading the young, they have only just reached Luoyang—no house with a single rafter, no stores of a dou of grain.

sentences.zh: 又冬月垂盡，東作將起，乃『百堵皆興』、『俶載南畝』之時，而驅之使擐甲執兵，泣當白刃，殆非歌舞之師也。

translations.literal: moreover winter month nearly ended, spring work about to rise, it is 'every wall rises' 'shouldering tools southern fields' season, yet drive them make don armor hold weapons, weep before bare blades, scarcely not song-dance army.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover winter is nearly ended and spring farming about to begin—it is the season of 'every wall is rising' and 'they shoulder their tools and go to the southern fields'—yet they are driven to don armor and take up weapons, weeping before bare blades; this is scarcely an army that sings and dances.

sentences.zh: 且諸軍已進，非無應接。

translations.literal: moreover all armies already advanced, not without support on ground.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the armies have already advanced—there is no lack of support on the ground.

sentences.zh: 若降款有實，待既平樊、沔，然後鑾輿順動，亦可晚之有！

translations.literal: if surrender has truth, wait until already pacified Fan, Mian, then imperial carriage in due order moves, also can be late!
translations.idiomatic: If the surrender is genuine, wait until Fan and Mian are pacified, then let the imperial carriage move in due order—not too late!

sentences.zh: 今率然輕舉，上下疲勞；

translations.literal: now rashly lightly move, above below wearied;
translations.idiomatic: To act rashly now wears out court and countryside alike;

sentences.zh: 若空行空返，恐挫損天威，更成賊氣，非策之得者也。」

translations.literal: if empty march empty return, fear damage Heaven's majesty, further strengthen enemy spirit, not policy's gain."
translations.idiomatic: if we march in vain and return in vain, we fear damaging Heaven's majesty and strengthening the enemy's spirit—that is not a winning policy."

sentences.zh: 司空穆亮以為宜行，公卿皆同之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Mu Liang held should go, nobles ministers all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Mu Liang held they should march; the nobles and ministers all agreed.

sentences.zh: 澄謂亮曰：「公輩在外之時，見張旗授甲，皆有憂色，平居論議，不願南征，何得對上即為此語！

translations.literal: Cheng said to Liang: "you gentlemen when outside, saw raise banners issue armor, all had worried expressions, ordinary discussion, did not wish south campaign, how obtain face sovereign immediately speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said to Liang, "When you gentlemen were outside and saw banners raised and armor issued, you all showed worry on your faces; in ordinary discussion you did not wish a southern expedition—how can you speak thus to His Majesty the moment you face him!

sentences.zh: 面背不同，事涉欺佞，豈大臣之義、國士之體乎！

translations.literal: face back not same, matter touches deceit flattery, how great minister's duty, national stalwart's bearing!
translations.idiomatic: Face and back at odds—this touches on deceit and flattery; is this the duty of great ministers or the bearing of a national stalwart!

sentences.zh: 萬一傾危，皆公輩所為也。」

translations.literal: if by chance overturn danger, all your gentlemen's doing."
translations.idiomatic: If disaster should come, it will all be your doing."

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「任城王可謂忠於社稷。」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Prince of Rencheng may be called loyal to altars and state."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng may be called loyal to altars and state."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「任城以從朕者為佞，不從朕者豈必皆忠！

translations.literal: emperor said: "Rencheng takes those who follow Us as flatterers, those who do not follow Us must all be loyal!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Prince of Rencheng takes those who follow me as flatterers—are those who do not follow me necessarily all loyal!

sentences.zh: 夫小忠者，大忠之賊，無乃似諸！」

translations.literal: petty loyalty, great loyalty's thief, perhaps resembles this!"
translations.idiomatic: Petty loyalty is the thief of great loyalty—does this not resemble that!"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「臣愚闇，雖涉小忠，要是竭誠謀國；

translations.literal: Cheng said: "your servant dull blind, though touches petty loyalty, after all is exhaust sincerity counsel state;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Your servant is dull and blind; though I touch on petty loyalty, it is after all whole-hearted counsel for the state;

sentences.zh: 不知大忠者竟何所據！」

translations.literal: do not know great loyalty ultimately on what rests!"
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what great loyalty can rest upon!"

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，發洛陽，以北海王詳為尚書僕射，統留台事；

translations.literal: xinhai, departed Luoyang, made Prince of Beihai Xiang Vice Director of Secretariat, directed rear capital affairs;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, he departed Luoyang; Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, directing affairs of the rear capital;

sentences.zh: 李沖兼僕射，同守洛陽。

translations.literal: Li Chong concurrently Vice Director, jointly guarded Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was concurrently Vice Director, jointly guarding Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎崔休為左丞，趙郡王幹都督中外諸軍事，始平王勰將軍宗子軍宿衛左右。

translations.literal: Supervisor Cui Xiu made Left Assistant, Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan commanded armies within without, Prince of Shiping Xie led imperial clan guard corps lodged guard left right.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Cui Xiu was made Left Assistant; Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan commanded armies within and without; Prince of Shiping Yuan Xie led the imperial clan guard corps to defend left and right.

sentences.zh: 休，逞之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Xiu, Chi's great-great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was the great-great-grandson of Chi.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏主至懸瓠。

translations.literal: wuchen, Wei sovereign reached Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, the Wei sovereign reached Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔壽陽、鐘離、馬頭之師所獲男女皆放還南。

translations.literal: jisi, edict Shouyang, Zhongli, Matou armies captured men women all released returned south.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, an edict ordered that men and women captured by the armies at Shouyang, Zhongli, and Matou were all released and sent back south.

sentences.zh: 曹虎果不降。

translations.literal: Cao Hu indeed did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu indeed did not surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏主命盧淵攻南陽。

translations.literal: Wei sovereign ordered Lu Yuan attack Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sovereign ordered Lu Yuan to attack Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 淵以軍中乏糧，請先攻赭陽以取葉倉，魏主許之。

translations.literal: Yuan because army within lacked grain, requested first attack Zheyang to seize Ye granaries, Wei sovereign assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, citing grain shortage in the army, asked to attack Zheyang first to seize the Ye granaries; the Wei sovereign assented.

sentences.zh: 乃與征南大將軍城陽王鸞、安南將軍李佐、荊州刺史韋珍共攻赭陽。

translations.literal: thereupon with General Who Conquers South Prince of Chengyang Luan, General Who Pacifies South Li Zuo, Jing Province Governor Wei Zhen jointly attacked Zheyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he joined with General Who Conquers the South Prince of Chengyang Yuan Luan, General Who Pacifies the South Li Zuo, and Governor of Jing Wei Zhen in jointly attacking Zheyang.

sentences.zh: 鸞，長壽之子；

translations.literal: Luan was the son of Changshou;
translations.idiomatic: Luan was Changshou's son;

sentences.zh: 佐，寶之子也。

translations.literal: Zuo was the son of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was Bao's son.

sentences.zh: 北襄城太守成公期閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Cheng Gongqi, governor of North Xiangcheng, closed the city gates and held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongqi, governor of North Xiangcheng, shut the gates and defended the city.

sentences.zh: 薛真度軍於沙堨，南陽太守房伯玉、新野太守劉思忌拒之。

translations.literal: Xue Zhendu encamped his army at Shayan; Fang Boyu, governor of Nanyang, and Liu Siji, governor of Xinye, resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhendu encamped at Shayan; Fang Boyu of Nanyang and Liu Siji of Xinye held him off.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏主遣中書監高閭治古樂；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei sovereign had sent Gao Lü, Director of the Palace Secretariat, to restore ancient music;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wei emperor had sent Gao Lü, Director of the Palace Secretariat, to restore ancient music;

sentences.zh: 會閭出為相州刺史，是歲，表薦著作郎韓顯宗、太樂祭酒公孫崇參知鐘律，帝從之。

translations.literal: When Lü went out to be governor of Xiang Province, that year he memorialized recommending Han Xianzong, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Drafting, and Gongsun Chong, Director of Sacrifices to the Great Music, to assist in pitch and regulation; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü was posted out as governor of Xiang Province, that year he recommended Han Xianzong, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Drafting, and Gongsun Chong, Director of Sacrifices to the Great Music, to assist with pitch and regulation, and the emperor agreed.
